title: Reduced Basis method for finite volume simulations of parabolic PDEs applied to porous media flows
abstractText: In the context of underground gas storage (of CO2 typically) in saline aquifers, numerical simulation is a highly valuable tool to evaluate the impact of the uncertainties of various model parameters and to optimize, e.g., injection-production scenarios. For this purpose, finite volume approximations of Darcy’s parabolic model for flows in porous media are usually run many times, for many values of parameters like permeability and porosity, at costly computational efforts. We study the relevance of reduced basis methods as a way to lower the overall simulation cost of multi-point finite volume approximations to Darcy’s parabolic model for flows in porous media for different values of the parameters such as permeability. We aim to quickly evaluate any linear form (or quantity of interest) of the pressure for many parameter values. To this end, we construct reduced bases by a standard POD-Greedy algorithm. Our POD-Greedy algorithm uses two new goal-oriented error estimators designed from a discrete space-time energy norm independent of the parameter. We provide some numerical experiments that validate the efficiency of the proposed estimators.

title: A cross-week analysis of urinary extracellular vesicles after respiratory tract exposure intervention in a cohort of isocyanate-exposed workers
abstractText: Background Urinary extracellular vesicles (EVs) are an accessible source of diverse molecular cargo with potential for noninvasive biomonitoring; however, the feasibility of recovering and characterizing their RNA and protein content from occupationally collected urine is not well established. This study aimed to evaluate whether urinary EVs isolated from field-collected samples could provide biologically informative molecular signatures and compared three EV cargo classes, RNA reads mapping to protein-coding transcripts (EV-mRNA-derived fragments), non-coding RNAs, and proteins, for their ability to distinguish paired sampling conditions and support exploratory biological interpretation. Methods Paired spot urine samples were collected from five workers in a fabric coating factory with well-characterized inhalation exposure to methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI) on Monday morning before and Friday afternoon after a one-week respiratory-protection intervention. EVs were characterized by morphology, size, concentration, marker expression, and proteomic composition. Total EV-RNA was profiled using a small-RNA sequencing workflow without size selection, enabling analysis of diverse RNA species and comparison of molecular cargo classes. Results Urinary EVs were successfully isolated and characterized from occupational field samples. Among the three cargo classes evaluated, EV-mRNA-derived fragments provided the clearest discrimination between pre- and post-intervention sampling conditions and generated candidate signatures for exploratory biological interpretation. The pre-intervention EV-mRNA-derived fragment signature showed nominal associations with inflammatory airway-related pathways and with hypersensitivity pneumonitis and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease profiles in the Integrated Human Lung Cell Atlas. These findings provide biological context but do not establish tissue origin, disease causation, or exposure specificity, particularly given the possibility of uncharacterized workplace co-exposures. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of urinary EV isolation and multi-cargo molecular characterization from occupationally collected urine samples. While EV-mRNA-derived fragments emerged as the most informative cargo class for distinguishing sampling conditions and generating biologically interpretable signatures, larger longitudinal studies are needed to validate these observations and define their utility for exposure-related biomonitoring.

title: Fourier-inspired automatic Cobb angles measurement for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
abstractText: Measuring Cobb angles in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) patients using anteroposterior (AP) radiographs is time-consuming and prone to variability due to subjective vertebrae selection. To address this, we propose an automated model for Cobb angle measurement using a Fourier-inspired method. The model starts by estimating the spinal curvature spectrum and then predicts the Cobb angles. We use a VGG-16 transfer learning model to regress the concatenated real and imaginary components of the spine's spectral representation. This feature is used to reconstruct the curvature through an inverse Fourier transform for improved model explainability. Simultaneously, it serves as input to a projection head for Cobb angle estimation. Evaluating on the MICCAI 2019 SpineWeb dataset, our model shows a Pearson correlation of 0.9382 for curvature estimation and a symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) of 12.25% for Cobb angle measurement, performing similarly to other top models. By treating spinal curvature prediction as a frequency domain analysis, our method offers more accurate curvature shapes than spatial domain approaches. Additionally, applying zero padding improves spectral resolution and reduces SMAPE in Cobb angle estimation. Spectral prediction consistently outperforms spatial prediction in both curvature and Cobb angle measurement.

title: The growth energy emissions trilemma: evidence from BRICS
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine the equilibrium relationship between economic growth, foreign direct investments (FDI), trade openness, fossil fuel energy use and CO2 emissions for Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS) countries over a period from 1990 to 2022. Design/methodology/approach Panel data tests are done using the first- and second-generation unit root tests, Pedroni and Johansen Fisher panel co-integration tests, fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) for long-run coefficient and the Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel causality test. Findings There is evidence of cointegration in the long run among the variables. According to the FMOLS estimates, fossil fuel energy consumption (elasticity = 0.847) and inward foreign direct investments (elasticity = 0.031) have a positive and significant effect on CO2 emissions, while trade openness has a negative but insignificant effect. Causality from GDP per capita to CO2 emissions (p < 0.05), and inward FDI to CO2 emissions (p < 0.10) is one-sided. Research limitations/implications The limitation of availability of data restricts the study period from 1990 to 2022. The study uses aggregate data on fossil fuels without differentiating the types of fossil fuels used. Further studies should consider the analysis with country-level asymmetry, structural break models and extended BRICS membership. Originality/value Built on the basis of the hypotheses of Environmental Kuznets Curve, this research attempts to combine the economic, energy, trade and environmental factors in one panel model for BRICS economies. This paper provides the long-run elasticity analysis and causality directions for green policymaking, filling the gap in literature that reports only about cointegration without the effect size estimates.

title: Landscape-scale predictors of mammal abundance and species richness across an extensive Queensland tropical savannas gradient
abstractText: The small mammals in the tropical savannas of northern Australia have undergone declines in recent decades; this is best documented in the Northern Territory. Data from northern Queensland are limited and although the same trends are assumed, the topographic and climatic features differ substantially. In this study, we examined data systematically collected from 725 sites between 1998 and 2012 in three bioregions representing a climatic gradient from semi-arid to monsoon tropical savannas. Using information-theoretic models and model averaging, we investigated the relationship between five mammal groupings (all mammals, critical weight range, macropods, rodents, and dasyurids) and three landscape variables (fractional cover green, elevation, and vegetation diversity) to elucidate any patterns in the mammal fauna across the Desert Uplands, Einasleigh Uplands, and Cape York. Key patterns included relationships with increasing elevation (critical weight range species richness positively associated with elevation, rodent species richness negatively associated), increasing rodent and dasyurid species richness with vegetation diversity, and lower macropod and dasyurids abundance with increasing fractional cover green. These relationships underscore a need to consider mammal conservation in Queensland with more nuance than in the more topographically inert Northern Territory. Management strategies need to be more attuned to taxonomic and regional differences, to prevent perverse outcomes.

title: The impact of external CEO appointments on firm strategy and risk
abstractText: Purpose This paper examines whether chief executive officer (CEO) origin is associated with risk-taking across innovation, financing, and organizational scope; how any difference changes over tenure; and whether the performance consequences differ by risk-taking channel. Design/methodology/approach We build a panel of 55,461 firm-year observations on US publicly traded firms from 2000 to 2024 by combining BoardEx executive histories with Compustat and Center for Research in Security Prices data. We measure risk-taking using three policy variables over which CEOs have substantial influence: research and development (R&D) intensity, leverage, and the number of business segments. We estimate industry- and year-fixed-effects models and supplement them with propensity-score matching and two instrumental variables based on the local supply of executive talent. Findings Firms led by external CEOs have higher R&D intensity, use more leverage, and operate fewer business segments. Matched-sample results are consistent with the baseline estimates, and the instrumental-variable analyses provide broadly similar evidence. The findings are not driven by the global financial crisis or COVID-19. The risk-taking difference generally weakens as external CEOs accumulate tenure. External CEO status is positively associated with Tobin's Q. Strategic refocusing is associated with stronger performance, whereas leverage-based risk-taking is associated with lower stock returns and industry-adjusted return on equity; the R&D interactions are not statistically significant. Originality/value The paper develops an organizational-identification and embeddedness account of how CEO origin relates to risk-taking, shows that the risk-taking difference generally narrows as external CEOs become embedded in the firm, and provides channel-specific evidence on the association between external CEO risk-taking and firm performance.

title: Intertwined charge density wave order in vanadium based kagome superconductors
abstractText: The discovery of superconductivity and charge density waves (CDWs) with multiple symmetry-breaking states in kagome superconductors A V 3 Sb 5 (A = K, Rb, Cs) offers a new territory for exploring correlated quantum phenomena. Here, we perform systematic measurements of elastoresistance in two hole-doped CsV 3 Sb 5 series: CsV 3-x Ti x Sb 5 (x = 0, 0.03, 0.05 and 0.09) and CsV 3 Sb 5-y Sn y (y = 0.04 and 0.06). The elastoresistance coefficient in all samples exhibits a discontinuous jump at the CDW transition temperature (T CDW), followed by an anomaly at a lower temperature (T*). Strikingly, T* displays an inverse relationship with the superconducting transition temperature (T c), suggesting a distinctive intertwinement. Using a Ginzburg-Landau framework, we attribute the jump at T CDW to a triple- Q CDW phase mainly driven by lattice instability. In contrast, the anomaly at T* reflects an intertwinement between triple- Q CDW and an incipient electronic order. Our present findings elucidate the interplay of electronic and lattice degrees of freedom in stabilizing intertwined orders and underscore the role of doping in tuning emergent quantum phases in kagome systems.

title: Kleene algebra
abstractText: This text is a set of lecture notes on Kleene algebra. It can be used as self-study material or as the basis for a graduate-level course, with exercises at the end of each chapter. In the text, we point out several subsets of the material that can be used for courses of varying levels, as well as several references to related research papers that can provide further reading material. Kleene algebra is the algebraic theory of regular expressions and was studied extensively over the last decades. We try to provide a comprehensive overview of the theory of Kleene algebra, including a completeness result. The completeness result relies on basics of coalgebra and automata theory, which are also included. Finally, we discuss the basics of Kleene algebra with tests, with an overview of its corresponding automaton model and a sketch of the completeness proof. We conclude the notes with a chapter on further reading and pointers to current research in the area.

Cognitive Management: A Systematic Explication of Applying Cognitive Sciences in Management
abstractText: Cognitive sciences have significantly advanced the understanding of human behavior; however, the systematic application of these insights in management remains underdeveloped. This study aims to articulate a comprehensive framework for applying cognitive sciences in management, spanning theoretical foundations to practical tools. Using a Systematic Review approach combined with qualitative content analysis, 40 scholarly sources from databases such as Scopus and Web of Science were analyzed. Findings indicate that Cognitive Management, as an emerging paradigm, organizes the application of cognitive sciences into five key axes: (1) management of cognitive biases (e.g., Devil’s Advocate), (2) choice architecture and nudge (focusing on the design of decision environments), (3) neuro-leadership (using the SCARF model to manage social dynamics), (4) cognitive load management (aimed at optimizing information and process design), and (5) cognitive AI (developing AI systems that interact with and complement human cognition). This framework suggests that, rather than attempting to alter human nature, Cognitive Management leverages the notion of bounded rationality to design environments and organizational processes aligned with the architecture of the mind. While this paradigm provides evidence-based tools that enhance decision-making, leadership, and human resource management, it also faces key challenges related to ethical considerations and the protection of individual autonomy.

title: Twenty-Five Years of Digital Governance Research (2000–2025): A Comprehensive Bibliometric and Science Mapping Analysis
abstractText: Digital infrastructures have become integral to public administration, but their rapid expansion has introduced governance challenges ranging from privacy breaches in sensor-based systems to uneven digital capacities across institutions. Although scholarly interest in digital governance has accelerated, the field remains theoretically fragmented, leaving its internal structure and developmental trajectory insufficiently mapped. This study addresses that gap through a bibliometric and science-mapping analysis of 2,314 Scopus-indexed publications produced between 2000 and 2025. Drawing on performance trends, collaboration networks, co-citation structures, and keyword-based thematic evolution, the study reconstructs how knowledge in this domain has clustered and transformed over time. The findings reveal a shift from early e-government and service delivery concerns toward broader socio-technical debates involving data governance, interoperability, civic digital literacy, and AI-driven accountability. Despite substantial growth, collaboration remains uneven and dispersed. Conceptual evolution indicates increasing integration of privacy, inclusion, and institutional capability as core governance mechanisms. The study provides a consolidated map of the field and offers implications for regulatory design, administrative capacity, and future research pathways.

title: Conceptual Framework for the Development of Digital Humanities Based on Artificial Intelligence
abstractText: This study aims to develop a conceptual framework for advancing Digital Humanities (DH) through Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. A systematic literature review was conducted using the protocol proposed by Kitchenham et al., combined with thematic analysis and guided by the PRISMA framework. Articles were retrieved from the Scopus database (2015-2025). The initial search yielded 544 articles, which were reduced to 20 articles after applying inclusion and exclusion criteria and screening for direct relevance to AI-based digital humanities research. The findings indicate that research in AI-driven digital humanities is predominantly data-driven and computational, with quantitative methodologies accounting for approximately 60% of the analyzed studies. Machine learning models, particularly deep learning and transformer-based architectures such as BERT, T5, CNNs, and LSTMs, were widely applied to tasks including text and image classification, topic modeling, and automated cultural data analysis. These approaches were frequently integrated with Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and knowledge graph–based representations, enabling context-aware and semantically enriched analyses of large-scale, complex, and unstructured cultural and historical datasets. The results also suggest an emerging tendency toward multimodal and hybrid approaches. Based on the analysis, seven core components were identified as the foundation of the proposed conceptual framework: deep learning and neural network models; NLP and structural analysis; cultural and archival data analysis; challenges and limitations; opportunities and benefits; computational resources and data requirements; and community engagement and ethical considerations. Overall, the findings suggest that AI can effectively augment human-centered approaches, offering a structured foundation for advancing research in digital humanities.

title: AI-Enabled Robust Performance-Based Budgeting: A Hybrid Neural–Optimization Approach for Smart Governance
abstractText: Performance-based budgeting (PBB) remains one of the most critical challenges in modern public expenditure management, particularly as governments transition toward data-driven and intelligent governance systems. Advances in artificial intelligence now allow budgeting processes to move beyond subjective estimates and toward analytical, transparent, and evidence-based decision-making. This study introduces an AI-enabled hybrid framework for PBB that integrates Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) with robust linear optimization to support smart governance and resilient resource allocation. The ANN component learns complex cost–activity relationships from historical organizational data and generates predictive estimates for future costs and cost drivers, which are among the primary sources of uncertainty in budgeting. These ANN-derived uncertainty intervals are then incorporated into a robust optimization model following Soyster and Bertsimas–Sim formulations to ensure both feasibility and optimality under uncertain conditions. The proposed hybrid model provides a transparent and intelligence-driven mechanism for allocating resources in alignment with organizational goals. The framework is validated within a major Iranian bank. Empirical results demonstrate that integrating ANN-based cost estimation with robust optimization significantly improves budget deviation indicators and enhances the accuracy, stability, and resilience of the budgeting process. The study contributes to the evolving field of smart governance by presenting a mathematically rigorous, AI-enhanced, and uncertainty-aware budgeting methodology.

title: Comparison of the LRFD Method and the Performance-Based Method in the Design of Mid-Rise Reinforced Concrete Moment Frames under Blast Loading
abstractText: In the design of structures, especially blast design, if the design method is not selected correctly, the proposed design may be uneconomical or unsafe. Since there is no method such as using behavior coefficient in blast design of structures, and the behavior coefficient available for seismic design of structures does not apply to the behavior of structures against blast. Therefore, this research compares the design using the LRFD method and the performance-based design in two 5-story reinforced concrete frames with a semi-buried reinforced concrete shear wall under a 10-ton TNT blast load located 30 meters away from the structure. Initially, the models were designed using the LRFD method by performing linear dynamic analyses. In the next stage, the aforementioned models were designed using the performance-based design method to provide three performance levels of uninterrupted operation, life safety, and collapse threshold. The results show that the acceleration value of all floors in the LRFD method is greater than the maximum acceleration values ​​based on the three performance levels (IO, LS and CP). Therefore, performance-based design, while being more economical than the LRFD method, also leads to a reduction in floor acceleration. Also, the performance analysis of frames designed using the LRFD method under explosive loading showed that these frames provide the IO performance level.

title: Acoustic Shield: Lightweight Neural Network for Audio-Based Drone Detection and Classification
abstractText: The widespread use of UAVs has intensified the need for advanced security measures to prevent unauthorized airspace intrusions and mitigate potential threats. Audio-based drone detection systems, which leverage the unique acoustic signatures of drones, offer a viable solution for remote monitoring and surveillance in sensitive environments such as military zones, secured facilities, and urban areas. In this paper, we propose a powerful framework based on a lightweight deep neural network architecture derived from ConvNeXt for accurate and real-time acoustic drone detection and classification. The proposed model is trained and evaluated on a diverse collection of drone and environmental audio recordings to ensure high performance and generalization across various conditions. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s outstanding ability to accurately detect and classify a wide range of drones in acoustically complex environments, while also maintaining low latency suitable for real-time applications. Moreover, the proposed multi-task model outperforms existing methods and proves to be a practical solution for deployment in resource-constrained audio surveillance systems. Despite achieving impressive accuracy about 99/55% in detection and 99/21% in classification, the model contains only 0/62 million trainable parameters (625542), making it highly suitable for integration into low-power, real-time environmental monitoring systems.

title: Design and Analysis of Scientific Networks on the Emerging and Safe Explosive Material (TKX-50) Using the Scientometric Software VOSviewer
abstractText: One of the fundamental principles of passive defense is the reduction of vulnerability of critical and military facilities against enemy attacks through non-armed strategies. Safe explosives, by mitigating unintended risks (such as accidental detonations or sabotage), contribute to enhancing the safety and security of infrastructures. The simultaneous increase in explosive power and reduction in sensitivity has led to the development of new generations of energetic materials. Among the noteworthy compounds in this context is dihydroxylammonium 5,5′-bis(tetrazolate)-1,1′-diolate (TKX-50). The primary objective of the present study is to design scientific networks of safe and emerging explosives (TKX-50) using the VOSviewer software. The methodology involves employing VOSviewer to analyze data retrieved from Web of Science, PubMed, and Scopus databases. The project is structured into seven stages: monitoring organization, search and collection cycle, analysis and meta-analysis, image updating, trend analysis and estimation, validation, and dissemination with feedback. Findings indicate that emerging explosives, as safer materials with reduced environmental impact and higher explosive performance, can serve as alternatives to currently utilized energetic compounds in applied industries. Examination of TKX-50’s functional properties reveals that its explosive efficiency is comparable to CL-20. TKX-50 demonstrates favorable compatibility with most components in explosive formulations, and in some sources, it is even considered a substitute for certain nitramines. Sensitivity assessments show that despite its high energy content and density, TKX-50 exhibits low impact and friction sensitivity, along with reduced toxicity compared to many conventional explosives. These characteristics highlight its potential for the future development of more efficient yet safer energetic materials.

title: Analyzing Cyber Threats and Vulnerabilities in Iran's Gas Industrial Control Systems and Presenting a Counter Measure System Model
abstractText: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) in the gas industry, as a part of the critical infrastructure of countries, are facing increasing cyber threats. These threats have created serious challenges due to the strategic importance of the gas industry in the national economy and security, as well as the very key role of industrial control systems in the gas industry. This research has been conducted with the aim of identifying and analyzing cyber vulnerabilities in the industrial control systems of the gas industry and presenting a systemic model to counter these threats. The research method is mixed (quantitative-qualitative), and the necessary data has been collected through field studies, in-depth interviews with experts, specialized questionnaires, and document analysis. The research results show that the main vulnerabilities include a lack of integration in the security architecture, the use of outdated systems, weakness in access management, and deficiencies in employee training. The proposed systemic model includes five protective layers (developed defense-in-depth) that, with an emphasis on a preventive and rapid response approach, can be implemented in the specific conditions of gas infrastructures.

title: Detection of Micro-UAVs in Visible Spectrum Using YOLO Algorithm
abstractText: The micro-drone, a type of unmanned aerial vehicle, typically measures only a few centimeters and is commonly employed in military operations and espionage due to its practicality. In recent years, the field has witnessed significant threats from micro-UAVs, prompting the need for effective countermeasures. The first step in addressing this threat involves developing robust identification methods. Advances in artificial intelligence and neural networks have significantly improved the efficiency and accuracy of micro-UAV identification techniques. Utilizing artificial intelligence, micro-drones that pose a security risk to protected areas can be identified on a daily basis. One of the most widely used artificial intelligence algorithms for identifying micro-UAVs in smart devices is the YOLOv8 algorithm. In tis study, experimental results conducted on the Roboflow dataset reveals that the YOLOv8 algorithm detects micro-drones with an accuracy of 95% and a speed of 30 frames per second.

title: GAN-Based Image Steganography Using EGD Architecture
abstractText: Steganography of a text across multiple images enhances security and prevents attackers from accessing the hidden message; moreover, generating multiple images with artificial intelligence also facilitates the availability of images for embedding each segment of the hidden text. This paper introduces a steganography system based on Generative Adversarial Networks that uses a three-component Encoder-Decoder-Discriminator architecture, the encoder extracts messages from steganographic images, and the CIFAR-10 dataset is employed for evaluation. This general method of “Generator and Encoder” combines a cross-entropy adversarial loss to fool the discriminator and a message loss to recover the message with the aid of the encoder. The main objective is to reduce the visible alterations in steganographic images compared to the original (Real) images and to enhance the recoverability of the message by the encoder, along with qualitative and quantitative evaluations such as SNR and BCE/MSE for message recovery. Experimental results show that, with proper hyperparameter tuning, messages can be embedded in images with minimal noise, and the message recovery exhibits low error and a desirable SNR. In the proposed method, at epoch 50, the SNR is approximately 34.9 dB. In this case, Loss_D is approximately 0.7 and Loss_G is approximately 1.2, which are suitable values for cross-entropy. The value of LossMsgLossMsg​ is approximately 0.03, which is considered excellent. It should be noted that the implementation in this article was performed using Python.

title: Passive Defense and Earthquake Risk Assessment in Urban Centers Using Linear Allocation Techniques (Case Study of Kermanshah Metropolis)
abstractText: Iran’s location on a major seismic belt, the high vulnerability of its cities, and the inefficiency of the existing crisis management system highlight the necessity of applying passive defense principles. This study aims to assess earthquake risk in the metropolis of Kermanshah by identifying and analyzing vulnerability components across four dimensions—natural, physical, social, and economic—using 44 specialized indicators. Data were collected through questionnaires and expert consultations and processed using GIS and LINGO software. The applied method was the Linear Assignment Technique, which enables the ranking of urban districts in terms of seismic vulnerability. The results indicated that Districts 7 and 3 exhibit the highest levels of risk, whereas Districts 8 and 6 show the lowest levels of vulnerability. Furthermore, the findings revealed that the spatial overlap of physical and social indicators with fault-line locations plays a decisive role in the severity of potential damages. Based on these findings, the key factors contributing to increased risk in critical areas were identified, and strategies aligned with passive defense principles were proposed to reduce urban vulnerability.

title: Optimization of the Number of Batteries and their Arrangement in Electric Vehicles Based on Multi-Objective Optimization
abstractText: In the design of electric vehicle battery packs, the optimal selection of parameters such as the number of series and parallel cells, the arrangement of cells, and their distance from the battery walls have a direct impact on the system performance. This paper presents a framework for the optimal design of battery packs that considers objectives such as minimizing cooling system consumption, controlling the maximum cell temperature, and optimizing the available space. This design is considered one of the key challenges in the production of electric vehicles due to its direct impact on the performance of the entire system and its importance in reducing weight, volume, cost, and increasing efficiency. The main innovation of this research is the use of the combination of the MOSOA algorithm to determine the optimal number of series and parallel cells and the MOGA algorithm to optimize the cell arrangement. Simulation results show that the proposed method reduces the battery volume by 22%, reduces the cost by 18%, increases the output power by 15%, and improves the temperature distribution by 10% compared to previous methods. This research can be a useful guide for the design and optimization of battery packs in electric vehicles.

title: A Simple, High-Order and Compact WENO Limiter Based on Control Volume for Spectral Volume Method
abstractText: The spectral volume (SV) method reconstructs a high-order polynomial in each SV from the cell averages of its control volumes (CVs). For discontinuous problems, however, a limiter is required to suppress spurious oscillations. This paper presents a novel CV-based high-resolution limiter that suppresses oscillations while preserving the subcell resolution associated with CV averages. Inspired by the SWENO method [47], we use nonlinear weights to reconstruct a high-order polynomial for each troubled target CV by combining the original high-order polynomial with several linear polynomials reconstructed from the averages of the target CV and its neighboring CVs. The resulting limited polynomial may be discontinuous across the boundaries of troubled CVs; therefore, numerical fluxes are used at these boundaries and at SV interfaces. At other CV interfaces where the reconstructed solution remains continuous, the physical flux is evaluated directly. The limiter is simple because only several linear polynomials are needed in the limiting procedure. It also preserves the compactness of the SV method and the resolution of CVs. Numerical results for one- and two-dimensional scalar equations and systems of conservation laws verify that the proposed CV-wise SWENO limiter preserves the designed high-order accuracy in smooth regions and is robust for problems with strong discontinuities.

Effects of calf neuromuscular electrostimulation on hemodynamics and systemic fibrinolytic activity: a randomized clinical pilot study
abstractText: Muscular physical exercise is a stimulus to circulatory development. But it is not always possible. In this context, there was the development of intermittent pneumatic compression therapy and, more recently, neuromuscular electrical stimulation. A clinical, interventional, prospective, single-center, randomized, single-blind study was carried out to evaluate the effect of neuromuscular electrical stimulation on lower limb hemodynamics and systemic fibrinolytic activity in 10 healthy subjects. The study protocol was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of the Botucatu Medical School, UNESP (CAAE: 30680120.0.0000.5411). The flow volume variation was significant, in the joint analysis of the limbs, at the popliteal vein. The diameter of the vessels proved to be the most sensitive to neuromuscular electrical stimulation in the joint analysis of the limbs. Flow velocities varied statistically significantly only in the femoral vessels. In the popliteal vessels, there was a variation in flow increment, but it was not statistically significant. There was no statistically significant change in the plasminogen activator inhibitor. For plasminogen activator, there was numerical variation, with continuous increment, but this did not represent a statistically significant change (p > 0.05). There was no adverse event and all subjects had the lowest tolerance score (no feeling of discomfort). NMES significantly improved popliteal and femoral hemodynamics. Although numerical increases in plasminogen activator were observed, they did not reach statistical significance (p > 0.05). The protocol proved to be safe and well-tolerated. Trial registration: Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC) RBR-6gs4bdh. UTN U1111-1301-5055. Registered on January 29, 2024. URL: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-6gs4bdh.

title: Full Frequency-Domain Inference for Weak FARIMA Models via Whittle Estimation
abstractText: This paper studies frequency-domain inference for weak FARIMA models based on the classical Whittle estimator. Although consistency and asymptotic normality of the Whittle estimator are by now well understood under weak dependence conditions, feasible estimation of its asymptotic covariance matrix remains a challenging issue in non-Gaussian and dependent settings. In weak FARIMA models, the limiting covariance matrix is not determined solely by the spectral density, but also depends on the fourth-order dependence structure of the innovation process through its trispectrum. The main contribution of this paper is to construct a consistent estimator of this asymptotic covariance matrix, thereby making feasible asymptotic inference possible for the Whittle estimator. In doing so, we address, within the FARIMA framework, the issue left open by Shao (2010) concerning the practical estimation of the limiting covariance matrix in weak time series models. The proposed approach adapts and extends earlier trispectrum-based methods, originally developed for observable short-memory processes, to the more delicate setting where the relevant fourth-order structure is associated with unobservable innovations and must therefore be recovered through residuals. We establish the consistency of the resulting covariance estimator and illustrate its finite-sample performance by Monte Carlo experiments.

title: Real-world solutions for real-world settings: effects of storage conditions on Streptococcus pneumoniae detection
abstractText: Background Appropriate storage and transport conditions are crucial for ensuring bacterial viability within biological specimens. Nasopharyngeal carriage studies are common for Streptococcus pneumoniae. However, storing or transporting specimens at ultra-low temperatures as recommended by the World Health Organization is not possible in all settings. Here, we assess the impact of alternative storage conditions on pneumococcal viability and density using laboratory-prepared samples. Methods Flocked swabs were inoculated with low (n = 395) or medium (n = 395) loads of single pneumococcal isolates. Twenty different serotypes were tested. Swabs were stored in skim milk, tryptone, glucose and glycerol (STGG) medium at -80°C (gold standard), -20°C and 4°C, and in silica desiccant packets (SDPs) at 4°C and 30°C. Viable counts were performed at inoculation (baseline), and 2, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days post storage. A subset of samples from baseline and 28 days post storage were assessed for pneumococcal detection and density using culture-independent, molecular methods. Results Using culture-based methods, pneumococcal recovery was high (≥ 80%) up to 28 days when samples were stored at -20°C and − 80°C in STGG. Samples stored at 4°C in both STGG and SDPs had inconsistent recovery (< 80%) by 28 days, and samples stored at 30°C in SDPs had very low recovery (< 15%) at all timepoints. Overall, when compared by culture to the inoculum load, density was substantially reduced when alternative storage conditions were used. When density was assessed by lytA qPCR, pneumococci could be detected for most (99%) samples in select storage conditions. Conclusions Improper storage of specimens may lead to underestimations of pneumococcal prevalence and density, especially when culture-based methods are used. Given this, study outcomes and methods of testing should be considered when determining feasible transport and storage conditions. We identified alternative storage conditions to the gold standard that could enable studies in remote or complex settings.

title: Anisotropy and tracer-profile assumptions in aperture-based strong-lens dynamics. Conditional inference from supernova distance ratios and unresolved stellar kinematics
abstractText: Single-aperture stellar kinematics jointly constrain the mass distribution, tracer light profile, and velocity anisotropy. Their coupling affects the interpretation of an inferred anisotropy. We quantify how tracer-profile assumptions and data treatment affect common-anisotropy comparisons and inferred mass-density slopes in a compiled galaxy-scale lens sample. We analyzed 107 lenses using distinct supernova counterparts, spatial flatness, distance duality, and the full supernova covariance. We compared the individual-slope power-law tracer with Hernquist and Sérsic profiles using measured effective radii. Numerical Jeans solutions, likelihood comparisons, posterior distributions, and controlled recovery experiments quantified the effects of tracer representation. The power-law fixed-minus-free Bayesian information criterion differences are 6.74 for isotropy and 41.51 for fixed β=0.18, compared with -3.89 and -2.26 for Hernquist and -4.67 and -4.30 for Sérsic n=4. The preference also changes with the Sérsic index. Removing 12 systems with a linearized distance-ratio uncertainty of above 20% reduces the power-law isotropy comparison to 2.51. In isotropic Sérsic n=4 and Hernquist simulations, power-law fits yield Δ _0>6 in 60.0% and 50.0% of realizations, respectively, compared with 0.5% and 1.0% for matched-tracer fits. BIC The preference for a common free anisotropy parameter depends on the tracer representation and sample composition. Controlled recovery identifies tracer mismatch as one mechanism that can generate this preference within the adopted aperture models. Physical interpretation requires a joint treatment of photometry, distance uncertainties, and kinematic weighting.

title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Fluorinated Usnic Acid Derivatives with Antibacterial and Antitumor Activities
abstractText: Usnic acid, a natural dibenzofuran product isolated from lichens, exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial and antiproliferative activities. Fluorination, as a modification strategy, may improve the biological activity of natural product scaffolds. Accordingly, we designed and synthesized 22 novel derivatives via introduction of a chlorotrifluoroethyl group at the C-17 hydroxyl position, followed by further structural diversification via Mannich condensation, enamine formation, and cyclization reactions. All target compounds were characterized by NMR spectroscopy and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). Their antibacterial activities were evaluated against Staphylococcus aureus, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), Bacillus subtilis, and Escherichia coli using disk diffusion and microdilution broth methods, while their antiproliferative effects were assessed against five human cancer cell lines (K562, A549, HepG2, MDA-MB-231, and SW480) via MTS assay. The results demonstrated that introduction of the chlorotrifluoroethyl moiety enhanced both antibacterial and antitumor activities. Among the derivatives, compound 3b exhibited the most potent antibacterial activity with MIC values of 2.5, 2.5, and 1.25 μg/mL against S. aureus, MRSA, and B. subtilis, respectively. Compounds 3f and 3h displayed broad-spectrum antitumor activity with inhibition rates exceeding 92% against all five cancer cell lines at 40 μM, and IC50 values as low as 10.07 ± 0.09 μM (SW480) and 13.38 ± 0.40 μM (A549). Structure–activity relationship analysis revealed that enamine derivatives of fluorinated usnic acid exhibited superior bioactivity, whereas cyclized isoxazole and pyrazole analogues showed diminished effects. This study successfully established an effective fluorination-based modification strategy for usnic acid, providing lead compounds and structural insights for the further development of usnic acid derivatives.

title: Beyond self-similarity: Reconciling X-ray scaling relations in galaxy clusters and groups
abstractText: Scaling relations hold among observed quantities that describe the thermodynamic properties of the gas in galaxy clusters and groups. However, observed data show systematic departures from the self-similar model's baseline predictions, particularly in lower-mass systems. I show that the observed departures from self-similar predictions can be efficiently described by two physical quantities modeled with power laws: the gas mass fraction (f_g ∼ T^ f_1 E_z^ f_z ) and the temperature variation (f_T ∼ T^ t_1 E_z^ t_z ). These phenomenological parameters allow us to compact all X-ray scaling relations into a single generalized form. Using a wide range of published X-ray scaling relations, this study conducts a Markov chain Monte Carlo--based meta-analysis to constrain the temperature- and redshift-dependence of the meta-parameters f_g and f_T and calibrate the model. These calibrations indicate that, while the gas mass fraction (f_g) does not show significant evolution with cosmic time (f_z = -0.11 ± 0.03), it decreases significantly with decreasing halo mass (f_1 = 0.50 ± 0.01). On the other hand, the temperature variation (f_T) shows a mild positive increase with both mass and redshift (t_1 = 0.15 ± 0.01; t_z = 0.11 ± 0.07). A systematic uncertainty of ∼ 0.05 can be assigned to f_1 and t_1, reflecting residual differences in instrument calibration, whereas statistical errors remain dominant for f_z and t_z. Overall, modeling the departures from the self-similar model with = L^ f_T drastically improves predictive accuracy, reducing the number of scaling relations in $>3σ$ ($>5 σ$) tension from 49 (36) percent under the self-similar scenario to just 8 (3) percent (three and one out of 39, respectively) that might be identified for their peculiarity. By imposing a minimal relative statistical error of 3 (5) percent on the published relations, I reduce the number of relations in tension at $>3σ$ to two (none). Moreover, modeling through this generalized framework allows for an extended discussion of the expected slopes and redshift evolution for several X-ray scaling laws, including the new quantity Y_ LGT0 -1 M_g^2 T^ a_L , a proxy for the cluster's volume that is independent of f_g and f_T by construction, and is predicted to scale directly with mass with a well-defined redshift evolution (M ∼ Y_ LGT0 f_g^0 f_T^0 E_z^2), as validated against hydrodynamical simulations and observational constraints.

title: Constructing professional chef identity through talent, creativity, and popularity: Insights from professional chefs
abstractText: Culinary literature often treats talent, creativity, and popularity separately, despite their growing importance in contemporary gastronomy. This study examines how professional chefs integrate these dimensions in constructing their professional identities. Using a generic qualitative inquiry approach, the study conducted semi-structured interviews with 15 professional chefs and mapped their perspectives through combined deductive and inductive qualitative content analysis. The findings show that chef identity is continuously constructed through three interdependent dimensions. Talent provides the technical foundation, creativity enables aesthetic differentiation, and popularity fosters social validation and peer recognition. The study offers an empirically grounded, descriptive framework that addresses this fragmentation. It shows how chefs navigate tensions among kitchen operations, artistic expression, and public visibility, and how they translate technical craft and creative ideas into recognized social capital in a competitive, media-driven environment.

title: Predisposition of galaxy clusters to producing exotic hyperbolic umbilic lensing configurations
abstractText: Strong gravitational lensing is a powerful tool for investigating the universe's large-scale structure and understanding the properties of dark matter and dark energy. The magnification and distortion of distant background sources by cluster lenses have enabled detailed studies of both lens and source populations, making these systems promising probes for precision cosmology. While classical strong-lenses are well understood, much remains to be explored for hyperbolic-umbilic (HU) exotic lenses, which produce unique telescopic effects and uncommon images with potentially very high magnifications. Identifying and quantifying these objects, along with characterising their geometric configurations, could have broad implications for studies of galaxy clusters and lensed galaxy populations. z<10 ). Finally, we estimate that each cluster contributes ( galaxies to its exotic volume on average (as a conservative lower bound), meaning that observing 19 clusters yields a 90% chance of detecting at least one HU system in a random sample.

title: The adversarial robustness of sketching and streaming algorithms
abstractText: Sketching and streaming algorithms are vital for handling massive datasets. While classical methods guarantee correctness on fixed inputs, they often fail with adaptive inputs, where future data depends on past algorithm outputs. This is common in settings such as optimization, databases, finance, and network monitoring. This monograph surveys recent advances in adversarial robustness, including techniques for insertion-only streams, connections to differential privacy, cryptographic methods that achieve adversarial robustness, and recent new techniques for robustness on streams with insertions and deletions. The authors also discuss fundamental limitations, especially for linear sketches and streams with insertions and deletions, where robustness often requires polynomial space or sketching dimension, and compare these to the recent techniques that circumvent these barriers using nonlinear algorithms. Throughout, this study explores core problems such as adaptively answering queries for optimization problems, norm estimation, frequency moments, and heavy hitters, and highlights emerging tools and open challenges at the intersection of streaming, sketching, privacy, and adversarial robustness.

title: Lightning in a bottle: theorising spontaneity as improvisational practice
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to theorise how spontaneity operates as skilled improvisational practice within consumption experiences, moving beyond its characterisation as mere absence of planning. Design/methodology/approach A 14-month ethnography of live grassroots stand-up comedy in Liverpool: participant observation at 28 shows, depth interviews with 10 comedian-audience members and informal interviews with 26 others. The lead researcher also performed stand-up. Analysis was iterative and hermeneutic. Findings Spontaneity operates through three interdependent dynamics: singularity (creating irreproducible encounters), sociality (building connections through collaborative navigation of unscripted situations) and speculation (engaging productive uncertainty that authenticates spontaneity). Rather than occurring naturally, spontaneity emerges through cultivated improvisational competence. Both performers and audiences perform essential labour in co-producing spontaneous moments, with genuine risk of failure constitutive of spontaneity’s credibility. Research limitations/implications Our focus on performer perspectives provides insight into producing spontaneity, though future research could examine how non-performing consumers navigate it differently. This study provides a framework for understanding how improvisational practice shapes consumption experiences across contexts requiring fluid response to unpredictable circumstances. Practical implications Practitioners cannot script spontaneity, but they can cultivate conditions for it to emerge. Training should develop improvisational competence, the capacity to respond fluidly to unscripted situations, rather than enforce rigid service scripts. Providers should recognise that consumers perform essential labour in co-producing spontaneous moments; creating space for audience contribution matters as much as performer skill. Experience designers should also consider that spontaneity privileges those comfortable with uncertainty, potentially excluding consumers who prefer predictable encounters. Originality/value Spontaneity is typically treated as the absence of planning, something that simply happens to an experience. This study shows the opposite: it is skilled labour, cultivated yet genuinely unrehearsed and co-produced, with audiences helping to make it rather than merely witnessing it. This study further shows that the risk of public failure is not a hazard to be managed but the very thing that authenticates the spontaneous moment. In doing so the authors answer calls to specify the theoretical architecture of consumption experience and extend work on experiential labour’s resistance to commodification.

title: Cosmic CORALS: Timing the Universe with high-z star clusters
abstractText: In this work, we explore the potential of anchoring the age--redshift relation across cosmic time by probing the oldest star clusters at high redshifts, now observed thanks to the Space Telescope in strongly lensed fields. As a case study, we consider one of the highest-redshift systems observed, the Cosmic Gems arc at z=9.625. We performed image deconvolution of multi-band JWST imaging, identifying a total of 20 point sources along the arc. We derived the stellar ages through a cosmology-independent spectral energy distribution fitting framework, ensuring that these measurements can be used as unbiased cosmological anchors. By combining these high-z systems with state-of-the-art local globular cluster ages, we performed a joint Bayesian fit to the age--redshift relation in a flat Λ cold dark matter model, measuring H_0=70^ James Webb +27 _ -16 km -1 Mpc^ -1 and Ω_m=0.33^ +0.37 _ -0.21 . While these constraints are still loose, we show that the slope of the degeneracy, a power law in the Ω_m - H_0 plane, is highly dependent on the redshift of the sources, becoming shallower as redshift increases. Leveraging this geometric rotation, we present forecasts showing that a future sample of ∼ 300 lensed proto-globular clusters well distributed up to z ≈ 10 could tighten the statistical precision to 4% on H_0 and 11% on Ω_m; this is competitive with and independent of methods currently in use. The present work, therefore, represents a new avenue in cosmology and comes at a timely moment, when JWST is observing high-redshift lensed star clusters routinely and and the Space Telescope are uncovering new strong lensing fields, and close to the start of operation of the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. title: The X-ray catalogue of FGK stars within 10 pc: The coronal temperature-brightness relation explained with the RTV scaling law
abstractText: A comprehensive measurement of stellar X-ray emission has important implications for our understanding of stellar dynamos, exoplanet atmosphere loss, and evaporation of protoplanetary disks. However, the samples discussed in the literature are often biased and the X-ray properties reported in published catalogues are often not homogeneously derived. We present a volume-limited catalogue of X-ray detections of the FGK-type main-sequence stars within 10,pc, which properly accounts for stellar multiplicity and considers the instrumental effect of optical loading of the X-ray detectors. The FGK,10pc sample derives from a recent Gaia -based catalogue of all stars in a sky volume of 10,pc around the Sun from which we extract all stars of spectral type F, G, and K. To build the X-ray catalogue, we retrieved and analysed all observations from SRG (Spectrum Roentgen Gamma)/eROSITA and XMM-Newton for stars in the FGK,10pc sample, and we cross-matched the sample with ROSAT catalogues. After accounting for optical loading, flares, and multiplicity, we fitted thermal plasma models to the X-ray spectra to derive X-ray fluxes and coronal temperatures. The FGK,10pc sample comprises 60 stars and has an X-ray completeness of 95%. We present a detailed investigation of the relation between coronal temperature and X-ray surface flux and we find the result to be consistent with the ranges covered by different types of coronal magnetic structures observed on the Sun. The lower end of the temperature-brightness relation is defined by the Maunder minimum star HD,166620 and three other stars whose positions identify them as possible Maunder minimum candidates. We identify systematic differences between the temperature-brightness law derived from XMM-Newton and eROSITA data that we attribute to their different instrumental response functions. For the first time, we study the impact of variability, both short-term flaring and long-term activity cycles, on the evolution of coronal temperature along with X-ray brightness. With the exception of three stars, a remarkably small scatter is observed in the temperature-brightness relation across the whole FGK,10pc sample. A natural explanation of the empirical kT-F_!̊m X relation is provided by the Rosner-Tucker-Vaiana (RTV) scaling laws defined for solar hydrostatic magnetic loops. The small spread of the observed relation indicates a universal scaling between the length and filling factor of coronal loops. Three observed outliers to the relation are stars that deviate from this invariance of the ratio of loop length to filling factor for an unknown reason.

title: Internalization of ESQ Values in Building Entrepreneurial Character and Work Ethic: A Study on Sasirangan MSME Entrepreneurs in South Kalimantan
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the internalization of Emotional Spiritual Quotient (ESQ) values in building entrepreneurial character and work ethic among Sasirangan MSME entrepreneurs in South Kalimantan. The study is based on the assumption that entrepreneurial success is not only determined by technical and managerial competencies, but also by emotional intelligence, spiritual awareness, and cultural values that shape business behavior. The internalization of ESQ values is considered essential in strengthening entrepreneurial resilience, integrity, discipline, creativity, and ethical work orientation among local entrepreneurs engaged in the Sasirangan industry as a cultural-based creative economy sector. This research employs a qualitative approach using the Library Research method. Data were collected from scientific journals, books, theses, dissertations, and academic documents related to ESQ, Islamic entrepreneurship, work ethic, Banjar culture, and the development of Sasirangan MSMEs. The collected data were analyzed through content analysis to identify conceptual patterns and relationships between emotional intelligence, spiritual intelligence, entrepreneurial character, and work ethic. The findings reveal that the internalization of ESQ values significantly contributes to the formation of entrepreneurial character through honesty, responsibility, discipline, emotional control, creativity, and social awareness. Furthermore, spiritual intelligence strengthens the Islamic work ethic by encouraging entrepreneurs to perceive work as a form of worship, thereby increasing motivation, perseverance, and professional integrity. Banjar cultural values such as kayuh baimbai also reinforce cooperation, solidarity, and collective responsibility among Sasirangan entrepreneurs. The novelty of this study lies in its integrative analysis of ESQ values, Islamic spirituality, and Banjar local culture in shaping entrepreneurial character and work ethic within the context of Sasirangan MSMEs. This research also offers a conceptual contribution to Islamic entrepreneurship studies by emphasizing the importance of emotional-spiritual intelligence and local wisdom as socio-cultural capital for sustainable creative economic development.

Floral nectary and pericarp galls of Sapium glandulosum: structural convergence and cell wall remodeling
abstractText: Galls are novel plant organs induced by specialized organisms that redirect host plant development. Although the host organ may impose structural constraints on gall formation, some gall-inducing insects can produce similar gall phenotypes in distinct plant tissues. Here, we investigated the morphology, anatomy, and cell wall immunocytochemistry of galls induced by Neolithus fasciatus (Hemiptera: Triozidae) in the floral nectaries and pericarps of Sapium glandulosum (Euphorbiaceae). Morphological and anatomical analyses were performed using historesin-embedded sections, whereas immunocytochemical analyses were conducted with monoclonal antibodies targeting homogalacturonan (HG) and rhamnogalacturonan-I (RG-I) epitopes. Gall induction in floral nectaries caused extensive tissue reorganization, including the loss of secretory epidermal organization, whereas pericarp galls developed from the exocarp and parenchymatous mesocarp. Despite originating from anatomically and functionally distinct organs, both gall types exhibited a remarkably similar structural organization, consisting of a uniseriate epidermis, a compartmentalized cortex with outer chlorophyllous parenchyma and inner parenchyma, collateral vascular bundles, laticifers, and a single nymphal chamber. Immunocytochemical analyses revealed a predominance of highly methyl-esterified HGs in both gall systems, indicating the maintenance of flexible cell walls. In addition, RG-I containing (1→4)-β-D-galactan side chains were particularly abundant in the inner cortex of the galls. These findings demonstrate that N. fasciatus exerts strong control over gall morphogenesis, driving anatomical convergence across galls arising from distinct plant origin sites while retaining origin-specific signatures in the cell wall pectic composition.

title: Survei Kepuasan Mahasiswa terhadap Layanan Program Studi Magister Manajemen FEB Universitas Trisakti 2024/2025
abstractText: Student satisfaction is an important indicator in evaluating the quality of higher education services because it reflects the extent to which the services provided by the study program align with student expectations. Therefore, periodic evaluation is necessary as a basis for service improvement and quality enhancement. This study aims to analyze student satisfaction with the services provided by the Master of Management Study Program, Faculty of Economics and Business, Trisakti University. The study employed a quantitative approach using a descriptive survey method. Primary data were collected through questionnaires distributed to active students who had received academic and non-academic services. Sampling was carried out using a purposive sampling technique, with 91 respondents from five study concentrations. The results show that, in general, students had a good level of satisfaction with the services provided by the study program, with an overall mean score of 3.52 on a 4-point scale. A total of 81.3% of respondents stated that they were satisfied, indicating that academic services, administration, student affairs, and facilities generally have supported the learning process. Nevertheless, several aspects still need improvement, especially the responsiveness of academic administrative services, accessibility of student activity facilities, and certain supporting facilities. This study concludes that the service quality of the Master of Management Study Program, Faculty of Economics and Business, Trisakti University, is generally in the good and satisfactory category; however, the survey results should be used continuously as a basis for service quality improvement.

title: Pengaruh Gaya Kepemimpinan Laissez-Faire, Lingkungan Kerja Nonfisik, dan Motivasi Kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan melalui Kepuasan Kerja pada PT Shield On Service (SOS)
abstractText: Employee performance is an important aspect in service companies because it is directly related to target achievement and service quality. At PT Shield On Service (SOS), the 2025 Key Performance Indicator (KPI) data show that several performance achievements remain below the 100% target, indicating the need to examine the factors influencing them. This study aims to analyze the effects of laissez-faire leadership style, non-physical work environment, and work motivation on employee performance, with job satisfaction as a mediating variable. The study uses a quantitative associative approach with 105 employees as respondents through a saturated sampling technique. Data were collected using a Likert scale questionnaire with five response options and analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4.1. The results show that laissez-faire leadership style has no significant effect on job satisfaction, but it has a positive and significant effect on performance. The non-physical work environment has a positive and significant effect on job satisfaction, but no direct effect on performance. Work motivation has a positive and significant effect on both job satisfaction and performance, while job satisfaction has a positive and significant effect on performance. Job satisfaction only mediates the effect of the non-physical work environment on performance. The novelty of this study lies in the simultaneous examination of these three factors and the comparison of direct and indirect paths through job satisfaction in a service company setting.

title: Pengaruh Pemberdayaan UMKM, Pelayanan Prima, Promosi, dan Literasi Digital terhadap Kinerja UMKM Berkelanjutan
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of empowering Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) through excellent service, promotion, and digital literacy on MSME performance. The study used a quantitative approach involving 100 MSME respondents. Data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using validity tests, reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination. The results show that MSME empowerment, excellent service, promotion, and digital literacy do not partially have a significant effect on MSME performance, with significance values of 0.177, 0.258, 0.629, and 0.653, respectively. Simultaneously, the four variables also do not show a significant effect on MSME performance, with an F value of 2.077 and a significance value of 0.090. The R Square value of 0.080 indicates that the model explains 8.0% of the variation in MSME performance, while the remaining 92.0% is explained by other factors outside the model. These findings indicate that increasing empowerment capacity, service quality, promotion, and digital literacy does not automatically improve MSME performance. Therefore, MSME empowerment needs to be carried out integratively through strengthening business management, implementing digital technology, marketing strategies, customer service, and continuous assistance so that the knowledge and skills gained can be transformed into business capabilities that generate economic value.

title: Analisis Pengaruh Kepemimpinan Transformasional, Komitmen Organisasi, dan Keterikatan Kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan PT Indocement Plant 11–14 dengan Iklim Organisasi sebagai Variabel Mediasi
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the effect of transformational leadership, organizational commitment, and work engagement on employee performance at Plant 11–14 of PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa, with organizational climate serving as a mediating variable. Field observations indicate that employee performance has not yet been optimal, as reflected by less inspiring leadership, weak emotional commitment, and low work engagement. The study population consisted of 395 employees, with a sample of 199 respondents determined using the Slovin formula. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using SEM-PLS with SmartPLS 4.1. The main findings show that transformational leadership, organizational commitment, and work engagement have a positive effect on organizational climate. Work engagement and organizational climate have a positive and significant effect on employee performance, whereas transformational leadership and organizational commitment do not have a significant direct effect. Furthermore, the mediation analysis reveals that organizational climate mediates the influence of the three independent variables on employee performance. Practical implications emphasize the importance of building a conducive organizational climate through transformational leadership, strong commitment, and optimal work engagement to improve sustainable productivity.

title: History of Intensive Care Nursing in Honduras
abstractText: Intensive care nursing is the nursing specialty that emerged to provide highly complex, specialized care to seriously or critically ill patients requiring constant monitoring and basic and advanced life support. Historically, its origins can be traced back to the triage of sick (soldiers) during the Crimean War, which led to a reduction in mortality. Later, the polio epidemic created the need to ventilate these patients, leading to the establishment of specialized units, particularly in Europe and the United States. In Latin America, nursing evolved with the creation of educational programs and the professionalization of the field. Specifically in Honduras, the history of nursing dates back to informal and religious care, followed by the establishment of nursing schools in the mid-20th century. It was formalized with the creation of the Nursing program in 1966 at the National Autonomous University of Honduras (UNAH). Since then, the nursing profession has evolved with the introduction of curricula and its expansion to other universities throughout the country. There is no exact, documented record of the date and hospital where the first Intensive Care Unit (ICU) was established in Honduras. It was likely a gradual process, influenced by advances in medicine worldwide. The first ICUs were probably installed in the 1970s and 1980s, as recovery or "shock" rooms in the country's main hospitals, such as the University Hospital in Tegucigalpa and the Mario Catarino Rivas Hospital in San Pedro Sula. The care of the most critically ill patients fell to nursing professionals who, due to their experience and dedication, acquired advanced skills and knowledge through daily practice and informal or on-the-job training (in-service education), because the formal specialty of intensive care or critical care nursing, as it is known today, did not yet exist. It is worth noting that by 1992,1 the Honduran Medical Journal, in a publication by Rafael Giovanni Perdomo Cruz, already defined the specialty of Intensive Care Medicine and its role, indicating that ICUs were already an operational and recognized reality within the Honduran health system at that time. This article aims to analyze aspects related to the history of intensive care nursing in Honduras. In conclusion, the history of intensive care nursing in Honduras points to an evolution from empirical practices toward a professional and specialized discipline grounded in scientific, technical, and technological knowledge, with an increasing focus on humanized care and continuous quality improvement, thus offering comprehensive care to patients.

title: Dampak Komitmen, Kompetensi, dan Profesionalisme terhadap Kinerja melalui Motivasi pada Pegawai Dinas Pemberdayaan Perempuan dan Perlindungan Anak di Kabupaten Tangerang
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the influence of Commitment (X1), Competence (X2), and Professionalism (X3) on Employee Performance (Y), both directly and through Motivation (Z) as a mediating variable, at the Department of Women Empowerment and Child Protection (DPPPA) of Tangerang Regency. The study was motivated by variations in employees’ levels of commitment, competence, professionalism, and work motivation, which affect the agency’s performance in implementing women empowerment and child protection programs. This research employed an associative quantitative approach using a census technique involving all 125 DPPPA employees as respondents. Data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire consisting of 44 statement items and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with the assistance of SmartPLS 4.0. The findings indicate that competence, professionalism, and commitment have a positive and significant effect on motivation. Competence, professionalism, and motivation also have a positive and significant effect on performance, while commitment does not have a direct effect on performance. Motivation fully mediates the effect of commitment and partially mediates the effect of competence, whereas its mediating effect on professionalism is not significant.

title: Approach for Dual Probabilistic Linguistic Decision-Making under Unknown Attribute Weights Based on Archimedean Power Muirhead Mean Operators
abstractText: Dual probabilistic linguistic term sets (DPLTSs) provide a powerful tool for describing uncertain, hesitant, and bipolar linguistic assessments in complex decision-making settings. Current aggregation methods for dual probabilistic linguistic information still have drawbacks. They can hardly mitigate the interference brought by biased assessment values and fail to capture the correlations among arbitrary attributes. To address these limitations, this paper develops a new class of dual probabilistic linguistic Archimedean power Muirhead mean (DPLAPMM) operators for multipleattribute decision making (MADM). First, by combining the advantages of Archimedean triangular norms with the power Muirhead mean (PMM) operator, the DPLAPMM operator and its weighted form are developed. The proposed operators can reduce the impact of unreasonable evaluation values while modeling the interrelationships among any number of attributes. Then, a dual probabilistic linguistic entropy is constructed to obtain objective attribute weights, which are combined with subjective weights to generate comprehensive attribute weights. Based on these results, a MADM method is established under a dual probabilistic linguistic environment. An illustrative case concerning industrial artificial intelligence (AI) project selection is used to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method, and comparative analyses show its flexibility and effectiveness over existing approaches.

title: Etiological Paradigm Shift, Sentinel Ocular Presentations, and Visual Recovery Dynamics in HIV-Associated Uveitis: A Retrospective Cohort Study at an Academic Referral Center in West Sumatra, Indonesia
abstractText: Background: Uveitis frequently serves as the critical sentinel clinical manifestation unmasking occult Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection. In the contemporary combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) era, shifting epidemiology has transformed opportunistic intraocular infections. Objective: To evaluate the sociodemographic profile, CD4+ immunological status, anatomical phenotypes (SUN criteria), infectious etiologies, and visual acuity outcomes in HIV-infected patients presenting with active uveitis. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Universitas Andalas Hospital, Padang, Indonesia (February 2023–August 2026), reviewing consecutive HIV patients presenting with active uveitis. Ophthalmic assessments included best-corrected visual acuity (LogMAR), slit-lamp biomicroscopy, funduscopy, ultrasonography, and serology. Visual changes post-targeted therapy were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Result: Seventeen patients (34 eyes) were enrolled, demonstrating striking male predominance (94.1%) with a mean age of 33.1 ± 7.6 years. Crucially, 82.4% (n = 14) were newly diagnosed with HIV at ocular presentation. Panuveitis was the predominant phenotype (70.6%), presenting bilaterally in 52.9%. Ocular syphilis (Treponema pallidum) emerged as the leading etiology (82.4%), followed by cytomegalovirus retinitis (11.8%). Post-therapy, the legal blindness rate (< 20/400) halved from 35.3% to 17.6%. Mean visual acuity improved from LogMAR 1.00 ± 0.91 to 0.74 ± 0.87 (p = 0.055). Overall, 41.2% of eyes improved, 50.0% remained stable, and 8.8% deteriorated due to irreversible macular scarring. Conclusion: Severe uveitis, particularly syphilitic panuveitis, represents an indispensable sentinel marker for occult HIV in young males. Routine reflex dual-screening for HIV and syphilis is strongly recommended in atypical uveitis, as prompt targeted therapy achieves substantial functional visual salvage.

title: Diagnostic Performance of the Eustachian Tube Dysfunction Questionnaire-7 (ETDQ-7) in Predicting Objective Eustachian Tube Patency Among Patients with Chronic Rhinosinusitis: A Cross-Sectional Analytical Study at a Tertiary Referral Hospital in Bali, Indonesia
abstractText: Background: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) can extend to the tubal orifice and cause Eustachian tube dysfunction. Concordance between ETDQ-7 symptoms and objective tubal patency in CRS remains uncertain. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ETDQ-7 for objective tubal patency impairment in adults with CRS in Bali, Indonesia. Methods: This analytical cross-sectional study enrolled 42 consecutive adults with CRS at a tertiary hospital from January to March 2026. ETDQ-7 scores ≥14.5 were considered abnormal. Tubal patency was assessed by acoustic impedance tympanometry. Chi-square testing, Spearman correlation, and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Result: Mean age was 38.9 ± 11.6 years; 57.1% were female. Abnormal ETDQ-7 scores occurred in 24 patients (57.1%), and objective impairment occurred in 26 (61.9%). Impairment was more frequent with abnormal than normal ETDQ-7 scores (83.3% vs 33.3%, p = 0.002). Scores correlated with impaired patency (r = 0.58, p < 0.001). Abnormal ETDQ-7 independently predicted impairment (adjusted OR 7.84, 95% CI 1.74–35.29; p = 0.007). Conclusion: ETDQ-7 is a useful outpatient triage tool for identifying patients with CRS who need objective audiological evaluation; it should not replace confirmatory testing.
