title: Research on the Development Path of Mass Choirs in Inner Mongolia
abstractText: At the present stage, China's mass choir activities face a prominent issue of an imbalanced age structure among participants. A significant amount of research focuses on elderly groups, while insufficient attention is paid to the growing demand for youth choirs. This paper selects the Hohhot Youth Choir as a case study. Through in-depth interviews with its founder, Teacher Wang Ruibiao, it deeply analyzes the unique social value of youth mass choirs in building youth social communities, alleviating mental anxiety, and enhancing aesthetic literacy. The research also reveals the practical difficulties they face in operation, including sustainability pressures from self-funding, differences in member turnover and musical foundation, and the limitations of the organizers' single-mode of "contributing out of love." To address these issues, this paper proposes a set of development paths for youth mass choirs centered on "attracting through diverse repertoire, implementing step-by-step training, community-based operation, and seeking external support." The aim is to provide a practical example for achieving intergenerational balance and high-quality development in mass culture. Youth mass choirs, as an important component of China's public cultural service system construction, have shown a robust development trend in recent years. Such amateur choir activities, mainly involving non-professional youth groups, have reached a considerable scale in major cities. According to the "National Mass Literature and Art Development Report" released by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism in 2023, by the end of 2022, there were over 53,000 registered amateur choirs of various types nationwide, with the proportion of youth-led choir groups increasing significantly. From specific practices, taking data released by the Shanghai Mass Art Center in 2024 as an example, among the city's 635 registered amateur choirs, youth participation accounted for 37.2%; among them, representative groups like the "Shanghai Youth Philharmonic Choir" regularly held public welfare performances, serving over ten thousand audience members annually. Statistics from the Beijing Cultural Center system indicate that among the more than 300 teams participating in the 11th Beijing Choral Festival and Mass Choir Competition held in 2023, youth choirs accounted for 41.5%, with over 13,000 contestants; among them, the specially established "Enterprise Employee Group" attracted many young professionals. These data fully demonstrate that youth mass choirs play an increasingly important role in enriching public cultural service provision and meeting the spiritual and cultural needs of youth groups, showing continuous growth potentcultural tourism performanceial.

title: From a mass invariant in a gravo-turbulent medium to the characteristic mass of star-forming cores
abstractText: The origin of the observed universality (or limited variation) of the stellar initial mass function (IMF) and its precursor, the prestellar core mass function (CMF), and thus of the characteristic mass of stars and cores across a wide range of different galactic environments remains an open, fundamental problem in astrophysics. In this paper, we demonstrate that we can explain this property from gravity and turbulence only, using a mass time-invariant that remains valid for a broad class of turbulent flows throughout the star formation process. This mass invariant is entirely determined by the large-scale normalisation of the field of density fluctuations in the Galactic interstellar medium (ISM), induced by turbulence. Using high-resolution numerical simulations, we first verify that the temporal invariance of this quantity is preserved in a self-gravitating turbulent medium. Then, introducing a self-consistent model of the statistical properties of the density field in the self-gravitating multiphase turbulent ISM, we show that the universality of the characteristic mass of star-forming cores is imposed by this invariant together with the scaling of the Larson relations. Our model successfully predicts the characteristic mass of the cores in Milky Way-like star-forming regions, as well as in more extreme environments such as high-mass star-forming regions and massive early-type galaxies. This scenario suggests that the characteristic mass of the CMF, and then probably the characteristic stellar mass, originates from a universal, fundamental property of turbulence and is imprinted both during the very early stages of the star formation process in the gravo-turbulent ISM, when the dynamics of the medium are still dominated by turbulence, and by the statistical properties of small-scale self-gravitating structures.

title: Rekayasa Ulang Proses Persediaan Barang Habis Pakai Berbasis Web pada Corporate University
abstractText: Consumables management at the Corporate University of PT United Tractors Tbk previously relied on paper forms and separate spreadsheets. This study analyzes process changes, functional acceptance, and model-based time changes through INCorp (Inventory Corpu), a web-based inventory management system. This retrospective case study applies an adaptation of the Process Reengineering Life Cycle, BPMN, Fishbone, User Acceptance Testing (UAT) documentation, and time analysis outputs from Bizagi. The changes include data centralization, integrated recording, digital approval, and report export, while physical inspection is retained. All 91 UAT scenarios comprising 237 steps were recorded as Pass. Under baseline parameters, model-based time reductions reached 44.37% for compliant goods receiving, 36.67% for normal requests, 33.22% for reporting, and 20.18% for stocktaking. Duration parameters are representative values based on observation, so results are sensitive to changes in these parameters. The contribution is a mapping of administrative process virtualization that retains physical controls and tiered approval in a corporate university.

title: Model Traceability Pangan End-to-End Berbasis Blockchain dan Arsitektur Hibrida Web2-Web3 untuk Program Makan Bergizi Gratis di Indonesia
abstractText: The Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) Program in Indonesia involves a complex food supply chain, spanning suppliers, inventory, production, distribution, and beneficiaries. This complexity requires a traceability model that enables integrated and auditable tracking of food histories across stages. This study aims to design and implement an end-to-end blockchain-based food traceability model using a hybrid Web2–Web3 architecture for the MBG Program. The study adopts a Design Science Research approach. The model uses batches as the primary tracking units, while the hybrid architecture separates operational data management in the Web2 component from the recording of traceability transactions through smart contracts on a private blockchain network. An initial evaluation was conducted through task-based testing and the System Usability Scale (SUS) with 10 participants. Of 33 task observations, 24 tasks (72.73%) were completed independently and 9 tasks (27.27%) with assistance, with no task failing. The mean SUS score was 67.25. These results indicate that the prototype can support the designed traceability workflow, although some tasks still require user assistance. The evaluation did not involve participants in the supplier role, so further interface refinement and evaluation involving all MBG stakeholder groups are needed.

title: Perbandingan Ketahanan Lintas-Domain Indobert dan SVM Pada Ulasan Game dan Media Sosial Berbahasa Indonesia
abstractText: Sentiment classifiers for Indonesian app reviews are rarely tested on any app other than the one that provided their training data. This study contrasts a linear support vector machine (SVM) with TF-IDF features and a fine-tuned IndoBERT. Both models were trained on Roblox reviews and then tested on held-out Roblox reviews as well as on Minecraft and TikTok reviews from Google Play. Each app contributed 2,500 class-balanced reviews, with labels derived from ratings. Performance was measured by macro-F1 with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and domain distance was assessed using five measures. On Roblox itself, IndoBERT and SVM showed no clear difference (0.867 vs 0.850). Across domains, IndoBERT scored roughly 0.065 higher and lost about 0.048 less. TikTok lay farther from Roblox on every distance measure and suffered larger drops, which is consistent with a distance effect. Domain-adaptive pretraining reduced the TikTok drop by 0.020 (macro-F1 rose from 0.794 to 0.810) but had no effect on Minecraft. In practical terms, IndoBERT is the safer option for developers who apply a classifier to other apps, while SVM is enough as a cheap in-domain baseline.

title: Co-invasion of the invasive Aporrectodea caliginosa and the newly recorded A. rosea (Crassiclitellata, Lumbricidae) in soils of southern Western Siberia: changes in soil salinity and water-soluble ion availability in a field experiment
abstractText: Secondary salinisation and solonetzicity of soils are among the most pressing environmental problems in Western Siberia, where saline soils occur in almost every administrative region. Bioremediation using earthworms is a promising alternative to costly conventional reclamation, but most evidence comes from laboratory studies. Two European invaders, Aporrectodea caliginosa and the recently discovered Aporrectodea rosea, inhabit the soils of southern Western Siberia. This study aimed to assess, through a field experiment at four sites, the effects of the two species on the ionic composition of the meadow chernozem solonetzic and solonchak soils and on the sodium adsorption ratio (SAR). We conducted the field experiment over 84 days on four plots in Omsk Oblast, using a complete randomised block design with four treatments: A. caliginosa monoculture, A. rosea monoculture, their association, and a control without earthworms. Cation and anion concentrations were measured by capillary electrophoresis. The effects of earthworms were layer-specific and species-specific. In monoculture, A. rosea significantly reduced SAR in the 20–30 cm layer, while A. caliginosa showed no such effect. The association of the two species resulted in a significant increase in potassium, magnesium, and calcium across all layers, an effect absent in either monoculture. These patterns are interpreted as a synergistic outcome of bioturbation by species that differ in their mode of action on the pore space. Our findings confirm the potential of A. rosea as a bioremediation agent for saline soils in Western Siberia and provide a basis for extrapolating the results.

title: Analisis Laporan Keuangan Untuk Mengukur Kinerja Keuangan Perusahaan Properti dan Real Estate (Studi Kasus PT. Deltacendana Citapersada)
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis kinerja keuangan PT Deltacendana Citapersada pada tahun 2025 serta membandingkannya dengan entitas induk (PT Jaya Real Property Tbk) dan rata-rata industri properti dan real estate di Indonesia. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah deskriptif kuantitatif dengan teknik analisis horizontal, analisis tren, dan analisis rasio keuangan (likuiditas, solvabilitas, aktivitas, dan profitabilitas) menggunakan data laporan keuangan tahun 2022–2025. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa PT Deltacendana Citapersada memiliki fundamental yang solid dengan pertumbuhan kas yang signifikan (92%) dan tren pemulihan ekuitas yang kuat. Dari sisi rasio, perusahaan menunjukkan keunggulan pada Cash Ratio (0,81) serta efisiensi operasional yang sangat tinggi, dicerminkan oleh Account Receivable Turnover (511,94 kali), Return On Assets (ROA 11%), dan Return On Equity (ROE 19%) yang jauh melampaui entitas induk dan rata-rata industri. title: Kampanye Digital Kesadaran Kesehatan Mental Melalui Media Sosial Bagi Remaja Di Jakarta
abstractText: Masa transisi dari Sekolah Menengah Pertama (SMP) ke Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan (SMK) merupakan tahap pentingdalam pertumbuhan belajar dan aspek psikososial remaja. Siswa yang baru masuk ke SMK menghadapi berbagaikesulitan, seperti memperkenalkan diri ke lingkungan belajar yang berbeda, menyesuaikan diri dengan tuntutan belajaryang lebih tinggi, serta menghadapi perubahan dalam cara berinteraksi dengan teman dan guru. Ditambah kondisi saatini yang membuat siswa terpapar media baru hasil digitalisasi. SMKN di Jakarta Utara sebagai lembaga pendidikan diwilayah DKI Jakarta menghadapi tantangan yang sama seperti yang lain. Kegiatan Pengabdian ini menggunakan metodepelatihan dengan teknik diskusi, ceramah, demonstrasi konten media sosial yang diselingi dengan games. Sehingga tidakmenjemukan bagi peserta, dan mereka dapat berkreasi menciptakan karya digital sebagai bentuk memanfaatkanteknologi media digital. Hasil kegiatan memberikan edukasi kepada siswa tentang kampanye melalui media sosial untukKesehatan mental untuk mencoba memproduksi konten Kampanye Digital Kesehatan Mental khususnya pada bidangpariwisata

title: Effectiveness of Human Resource Management in the Warehouse of PT Indotruck Utama, Medan Branch
abstractText: Kinerja gudang tidak hanya ditentukan oleh fasilitas dan sistem, tetapi juga oleh tenaga kerja yang mengoperasikannya. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan dan menilai efektivitas pengelolaan sumber daya manusia (SDM) di gudang PT Indotruck Utama Cabang Medan, perusahaan yang bergerak dalam distribusi, penjualan, dan layanan purna jual alat berat, truk, suku cadang, dan bus. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif. Data diperoleh melalui wawancara dengan kepala gudang, dilengkapi observasi lapangan sebagai pembanding keterangan informan, kemudian dianalisis dengan model interaktif (reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan). Efektivitas dinilai melalui enam fungsi pengelolaan SDM (pembagian tugas, perencanaan, penempatan, pelatihan, pengawasan, dan penilaian kinerja) serta tiga capaian operasional (ketepatan pencatatan, ketepatan waktu, dan keselamatan kerja). Hasil menunjukkan bahwa pengawasan, keselamatan kerja, dan ketepatan pencatatan berada pada kategori efektif; perencanaan dan penempatan, pembagian tugas, pelatihan, serta ketepatan waktu tergolong cukup efektif; sedangkan penilaian kinerja perlu diperbaiki karena belum memiliki indikator terukur. Kelemahan utama terletak pada seluruh pekerjaan pelaksana gudang yang bertumpu pada satu karyawan sehingga keterlambatan bongkar muat muncul ketika pengiriman menumpuk

title: Breaking the chain? – Social work resources buffering the impact of municipality size and poverty on emergency child removals in Finland
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to investigate how structural community-level factors – specifically municipality size and poverty – are associated with emergency child removal rates. It further explores whether the availability of social work resources moderates these relationships. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on data from 292 Finnish municipalities with emergency-removal rates averaged over 2019–2022 and a complete-case analytical sample of 281 municipalities, the study uses a moderated mediation framework to analyse the indirect association between municipality size and emergency child removals through poverty and how this association varies with social work capacity, operationalised as the client-to-social-worker ratio. Findings Municipality size was positively associated with poverty, but its adjusted direct association with emergency removals was not statistically significant in the full model. Poverty was more strongly associated with emergency removals where client-to-social-worker ratios were higher. The conditional indirect association through poverty was significant at average and high caseloads, but not at low caseloads. Originality/value This study contributes to the growing literature on structural influences in child protection by highlighting the moderating role of frontline social work capacity. It identifies staffing relative to client numbers as an important context for understanding municipal differences in the poverty–removal association. The findings inform discussion of equitable service provision, although the effects of staffing interventions require further investigation.

title: Beyond the track: visualizing family spectator experiences at the US Grand Prix
abstractText: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to explore mega-sports event tourism and the spectator experience through a case study of a family attending the USGP hosted COTA in Austin, Texas. Data were collected over two race weekends in 2022 and 2023 using visual autoethnography. Two researchers who were F1 fans offered emic insight, while the third, a non-fan, offered an etic perspective to maintain interpretive balance. Fan engagement, family attendees, and spectator discomfort emerged as key themes providing implications for understanding the F1 spectator experience and event management practices.

title: Artificial intelligence as recurring organizational change: accountability and management control challenges across AI waves
abstractText: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in organizational decision-making, raising questions about how decision authority, accountability and management control are allocated and maintained. This paper aims to examine why accountability and management control challenges may recur across different technological configurations. It proposes that such challenges can arise when changes in effective decision authority are not accompanied by corresponding clarification of organizational responsibility and opportunities for oversight and intervention. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a conceptual and interpretive research design based on a historically informed analysis of organizational change. Drawing on literature from management control, governance and organizational studies, it compares four waves of AI-related organizational change: computational decision support as a precursor to organizational AI adoption, followed by expert systems, data-driven and algorithmic management and contemporary AI-enabled environments. The analysis develops a conceptual synthesis of recurring accountability questions across these configurations. Findings The analysis identifies four recurring areas of concern: potential misalignment between effective decision authority and formal responsibility; limitations in decision visibility and traceability; insufficient integration of decision technologies with strategic management control; and governance arrangements that may require adaptation as systems and organizational uses change. These patterns are not presented as inevitable outcomes of AI adoption. Instead, the study proposes authority–responsibility decoupling as a mechanism through which accountability and management control gaps may persist or reemerge under particular organizational conditions. Originality/value The paper contributes to research on accounting and organizational change by connecting contemporary AI governance questions to a longer history of organizational decision technologies. Its wave-based framework distinguishes a precursor phase of computational decision support from subsequent AI adoption and links recurring accountability challenges to decision rights, responsibility, oversight and management control. The resulting conceptual proposition provides a basis for future empirical research and for examining how governance arrangements can be adapted to AI-enabled decision processes.

title: Evaluation of Early-Age Properties of Portland Cement-Based Systems in the Presence of Accelerating Agents Using Inter-Test Correlations
abstractText: This study investigates the inter-test correlation between various early-age characteristics of complex cementitious systems. The correlations are used for predicting physical and chemical processes in portland cement–based systems with different chemical and physical accelerators. Correlations were established between the heat of hydration (HoH), ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV), setting time, compressive strength, and hydrate phases for cement pastes and mortars. When controlling for accelerator type/dosage, temperature, or water-to-cement ratio, correlating HoH to UPV for cement pastes demonstrated R2 values >0.90, indicating reliability when controlled. However, when testing on mortar samples, a reduction in R2 to 0.75 was observed, marking the principal limitation of correlating these two tests. Predicting compressive strength based on HoH when controlling for the water-to-cement ratio or temperature resulted in correlations of R2 = 0.81 and R2 = 0.86, respectively. The main limitation was again when switching to mortar samples, which demonstrated an R2 of 0.66 at sand-to-cement ratio (S/C) = 1.5.

title: Fenomena Silent Treatment sebagai Bentuk Hambatan Komunikasi dalam Hubungan Interpersonal
abstractText: Interpersonal communication is a process of exchanging messages between individuals, playing a crucial role in building relationships, expressing feelings, and resolving conflicts. In practice, however, interpersonal communication is not always effective. One phenomenon that acts as a barrier in interpersonal relationships is the "silent treatment"—the act of intentionally ignoring someone by ceasing all communication, whether verbal or nonverbal. This phenomenon frequently arises when individuals encounter conflicts, disagreements, or dissatisfaction within a relationship. This article examines the silent treatment as a communication barrier, exploring the underlying factors and its impact on the quality of interpersonal relationships. The study employs a qualitative descriptive method, utilizing a literature review of relevant scholarly journals and books. The findings indicate that the silent treatment functions as a form of passive-aggressive communication that hinders openness, empathy, the provision of support, positive attitudes, and equality within a relationship. Furthermore, this behavior can lead to anxiety, confusion, diminished self-esteem, and a decline in both trust and emotional closeness. Consequently, developing skills in emotional regulation, assertive communication, and openness during conflict resolution is essential for fostering healthy and effective interpersonal relationships.

title: Professional and educational development for person-centred care and shared decision making in the integrated care system: the concept of power
abstractText: Purpose Person-centred care is a crucial component of realising the aspirations of integrated care systems, ensuring service users receive interventions tailored to their needs and efficient utilisation of health and social care resource occurs. To effectively achieve person-centred care, practitioners and leaders within integrated care systems are recommended to engage in processes of shared decision making through individual and collective stakeholder engagement, maximising the opportunity afforded by the legislation of integrated care systems in England and the necessary redesign of services to align provision with the needs of local communities and care recipients. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper presents the principles of person-centred care, shared decision making and stakeholder engagement through an ethical and values-based practice lens, advocating for the recognition of and redistribution of professional power to recipients of care as a cornerstone for effective practice within integrated care systems and as a core component for the development and education of health and social care practitioners. Findings The discussion conceptualises person-centred care and shared decision making as stakeholder engagement processes within integrated care systems and advocates for user empowerment as an essential activity for improving outcomes for individuals, their families, communities and wider systems through the provision of integrated care. Originality/value This conceptual paper offers perspectives on the criticality of realigning power dynamics within integrated care systems, to provide better contemporary service delivery to diverse populations through person-centred care and to guide professional development activities. The values-based lens of the discussion offers theoretical underpinning for decision makers, educators and practitioners to develop health and social care practice which centralises person-centred care through redistribution of power with communities.

title: The GAPS programme at TNG. LXXXIII. Orbital refinement and atmospheric investigation of TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b)
abstractText: TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b) is a highly irradiated ultra-hot Jupiter on a strongly misaligned orbit, making it a benchmark target for atmospheric and dynamical studies. We aim to comprehensively characterise the TOI-1518 system by refining its orbital and physical parameters, and by investigating the chemical composition of the planetary atmosphere through transmission spectroscopy. We employed a joint Bayesian framework combining TESS photometry, HARPS-N high-resolution spectroscopy, and least-squares deconvolution profiles to break stellar geometrical degeneracies. We then applied single-line and cross-correlation function (CCF) transmission spectroscopy across theoretical templates. title: Prevalence and pattern of adverse childhood experiences and their association with criminal behaviors among incarcerated individuals: a retrospective correlational study
abstractText: Purpose Adversity during childhood is recognized as a developmental risk for a range of behavioral problems and mental health issues across the lifespan. Few studies have been conducted in Pakistan to investigate the association between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and criminal behavior, particularly the relationship between specific ACEs and specific types of criminal offenses. This study aims to explore the prevalence and pattern of ACEs among incarcerated individuals and the relationship between ACE scores and the frequency and severity of crimes. Design/methodology/approach This quantitative study used a retrospective correlational design to collect data from 200 incarcerated individuals at Abbottabad District Jail and Central Prison Haripur. Participants (aged 18–60) were recruited using purposive sampling. Findings The findings of multiple response analysis showed that two-thirds of participants in the current sample were exposed to two or more ACEs, and all participants had experienced at least one ACE. Exposure to violence, both within the household and in the broader community, was highly prevalent. A chi-square test of independence showed that higher levels of ACE exposure were associated with higher crime frequency among prisoners. Cross-tabulation was conducted to assess the association between ACE types and crime types. Findings showed that violent and drug-related crimes were more commonly reported across several ACE categories. Practical implications These findings suggest that childhood adversity could be a risk factor for criminal offending in adulthood. This study highlights the importance of early identification of ACEs, advocating for the inclusion of trauma-informed approaches to prevent crime in the Pakistani context and to reduce the long-term psychological effects of ACEs. Originality/value This study examines correlations between specific ACE categories and various categories of criminal offenses; it offers context-specific evidence and fills a gap in the Pakistani literature. The results contribute to the international literature on the association between childhood adversity and offending and provide implications for the formulation of childhood adversity-informed policies for prevention, rehabilitation and criminal justice in Pakistan.

title: David versus Goliath: understanding how consumers navigate their relationship with a brand involved in online moral-panic dynamics
abstractText: Purpose Research on brand transgressions has primarily examined consumers’ emotional and behavioural responses at the individual level, yet little is known about how such transgressions unfold as collective phenomena on social media. This study aims to examine how consumers individually and collectively negotiate their relationships with brands during moralised online controversies, focusing on the escalation of brand transgressions into moral-panic dynamics and their implications for the consumer-brand relationship. Design/methodology/approach A nine-month netnography was conducted to analyse Reddit discussions related to the 2022 Balenciaga controversy. Approximately 800 conversational traces posted between November 2022 and August 2024 were unobtrusively collected from the 20 most active and content-rich threads across 16 relevant subreddits. Findings Findings provide evidence of both individual-level (relationship destabilisation, decoupling and rupture) and collective-level negotiation practices (relationship rupture amplification, rupture delegitimisation and reframing). A theoretically informed interpretation explains how consumer-brand relationships are simultaneously personally experienced and socially constructed. Originality/value This study advances brand transgression research by conceptualising moral-panic dynamics as a collective phenomenon unfolding across moralised brand controversies, shifting the focus from individual reactions to collective processes reshaping consumer-brand relationships in digital environments.

title: Pengaruh Loan to Deposit Ratio dan Capital Adequacy Ratio Terhadap Pertumbuhan Laba Bank Swasta di BEI 2019–2023
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR) dan Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) terhadap pertumbuhan laba pada bank swasta yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2019–2023. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan keuangan tahunan tujuh bank swasta. Sampel penelitian terdiri atas 35 observasi yang dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas, regresi linear berganda, koefisien determinasi, uji t, dan uji F dengan bantuan IBM SPSS Statistics. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa data berdistribusi normal dengan nilai Asymp. Sig. sebesar 0,200. Secara parsial, LDR tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap pertumbuhan laba dengan nilai signifikansi 0,481, sedangkan CAR juga tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap pertumbuhan laba dengan nilai signifikansi 0,734. Secara simultan, LDR dan CAR tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap pertumbuhan laba dengan nilai signifikansi 0,409. Nilai koefisien determinasi (R²) sebesar 0,054 menunjukkan bahwa LDR dan CAR hanya mampu menjelaskan 5,4% variasi pertumbuhan laba, sedangkan 94,6% dipengaruhi oleh faktor lain di luar model penelitian.

title: Diksi dalam Bahasa Indonesia: Kajian Konseptual Tentang Ketepatan, Kesesuaian, dan Implikasinya bagi Komunikasi Efektif
abstractText: Word choice (diction) is a foundation of every communicative event, because words carry ideas from speaker to listener. This conceptual article describes the nature of diction in Indonesian, formulates the dimensions used to assess it, and examines its implications for effective communication. Through a literature review that combines narrative review, qualitative content analysis, thematic synthesis, and conceptual framework building, applied to diction, theories of meaning, the cooperative principle, and politeness theory, the article argues that good diction goes beyond dictionary correctness and comprises four interrelated dimensions: accuracy, appropriateness, clarity, and ethics. In the digital era these dimensions are challenged by foreign borrowings, code-mixing, abbreviations, and euphemisms. The article proposes a concise conceptual framework applicable to Indonesian-language teaching, academic writing, and public communication.

title: Hill Dickinson Stadium for Everton Football Club: geotechnical dock preparation and infill design
abstractText: Everton Football Club’s Hill Dickinson Stadium has been built on the site of Bramley-Moore Dock, Liverpool. This paper focuses on the dock infill and the associated geotechnical challenges. A baseline option would have been to remove existing soft dock deposits before infilling. However, the alternative of retaining dock deposits prior to infilling was more sustainable and reduced the programme duration. Three locations were sampled for sea-dredged sand to infill the dock. Oedometer and triaxial tests were undertaken using preparation methods that replicated the proposed dock filling process (a) sand dynamically compacted at the surface (b) sand falling loosely through water but affected by compaction and (c) sand falling loosely through the water but not affected by compaction. Results of the different sample areas were compared and creep settlement of the chosen site-winning location was calculated. This was combined with settlement estimates of the dock deposits to conclude the anticipated total settlement during construction and stadium design life. The paper describes the analysis and design undertaken to prove the feasibility of retaining the dock deposits through quantifying the magnitude and rate of settlement during construction and the design life of the stadium.

title: Saturación de oxígeno y puntuación de Apgar durante la transición neonatal a gran altitud: estudio en Huancavelica, Perú
abstractText: In Andean cities, newborns adapt under hypobaric hypoxia, yet reference values for oxygen saturation come from sea-level studies. The aim was to describe oxygen saturation during the first ten minutes of life in healthy term newborns born at 3680 meters above sea level and to explore its relationship with the Apgar score. An observational, cross-sectional, correlational study was conducted at the Zacarías Correa Valdivia Regional Hospital (Huancavelica, Peru) between August and November 2017, including 101 healthy term newborns delivered vaginally. Saturation was measured by pulse oximetry on the right foot at one, five and ten minutes; the Apgar score and heart and respiratory rates were also recorded. Mean saturation increased from 69.7% at one minute to 77.5% at five minutes and 84.9% at ten minutes; half of the newborns did not exceed 85% at ten minutes. There were no differences by sex. Ninety-nine percent had an Apgar score of seven to ten at one and five minutes, and all of them at ten minutes. Saturation remained below sea-level reference ranges throughout the first ten minutes, even with a normal Apgar score, which supports the use of local ranges to guide oxygen therapy.

title: Exploring the impact of social gamification affordances on IT-embedded pro-environmental behaviors: a multi-goal perspective
abstractText: Purpose Prior research shows that gamification affordances and goal frames can promote pro-environmental behavior (PEB) in green IT. Yet the role of social gamification affordances and their relationship with normative concerns remains less clear. Drawing on affordance theory and goal-framing theory, this study examines how interactivity, competition and cooperation activate hedonic and social gain goals, and how environmental responsibility conditions their effects on IT-embedded PEB. Design/methodology/approach A two-wave time-lagged survey of Ant Forest users was conducted to examine how perceived social gamification affordances and goal activations relate to subsequent IT-embedded PEB. Findings Social gamification affordances promote IT-embedded PEB through self-oriented goals, but their effects vary. Interactivity strengthens both hedonic and social gain goals, whereas competition and cooperation operate mainly through hedonic goals. Environmental responsibility positively moderates the effect of hedonic goals on IT-embedded PEB but weakens the effect of social gain goals. Research limitations/implications This study extends gamified green IT research by explaining how social gamification affordances activate self-oriented goals and how normative concerns condition the behavioral consequences of these goals. Practical implications Platform managers should design social features that make participation interactive and enjoyable while aligning gamification mechanisms with environmental responsibility rather than relying solely on social recognition. Originality/value This study develops a process model linking social gamification affordances, hedonic and social gain goals, environmental responsibility and IT-embedded PEB, offering a fine-grained explanation of socially gamified green IT.

title: Estimating Unconfined Compressive Strength (UCS) of Rocks from Measurement While Drilling (MWD) Data Collected during Laboratory Rock Coring
abstractText: Measurement-while-drilling (MWD) technology enables the real-time monitoring of drilling parameters during the drilling process. MWD data can provide valuable insight into the mechanical behavior of intact rocks and rock masses, which is essential for geotechnical applications such as foundation design and underground construction. The aim of this study is to correlate real-time drilling parameters, recorded using a laboratory-developed MWD system, with the unconfined compressive strength (UCS) of rocks. A custom laboratory MWD system was designed to simultaneously record four key drilling parameters: thrust (axial force and crowd), torque, penetration rate, and rotational speed. The custom-built MWD system was used to continuously measure the drilling parameters while coring into five different materials: gypsum, sandstone, dolomite, basalt, and concrete. Core samples collected during these corings were then tested for UCS under both dry and water-saturated conditions. Two compound parameters—specific energy and drillability—were calculated from the raw MWD data and compared with UCS values. Both indices showed a good correlation with UCS, with specific energy providing slightly more accurate predictions. These results demonstrate the potential of laboratory-based MWD systems as practical tools for estimating rock strength in geotechnical investigations.

title: Touchdown or fumble: strategic talent acquisition in the National Football League
abstractText: Research methodology This case is based on multiple media reports before and during the Kansas City Chiefs’ 2024 season, specifically in early October 2024, after two of the Chiefs’ wide receivers were injured. Primary sources included YouTube recordings of interviews with Brett Veach, numerous Chiefs’ players and officials, various commentators discussing the team’s activities and the ESPN six-part documentary series “The Kingdom.” These were supplemented with various published, online and broadcast sports reports. The YouTube videos were transcribed using Transkriptor, a web-based AI application. The ESPN documentary audio “The Kingdom” was transcribed from closed caption text. A complete set of references is contained in the case footnotes and the teaching notes’ reference section. Case overview/synopsis Brett Veach, General Manager of the Kansas City Chiefs National Football League (NFL) team, needed to find an additional wide receiver. The Chiefs and most NFL teams typically had six wide receivers on the team. The Chiefs had only four wide receivers in early October after their top two wide receivers suffered long-term injuries and might not play again in the 2024 season. Veach had until the NFL’s November 5th trade deadline to identify a candidate and negotiate a trade with another NFL team. The Chiefs were trying to get to their third consecutive Super Bowl, a first in the NFL and had 12 more regular-season games plus up to three playoff games to play. Could Veach find an available wide receiver that could meet the Chiefs’ on-the-field needs, fit with the Chiefs’ culture and save the Chiefs’ chance at a third Super Bowl by the November 5th trade deadline? Complexity academic level The case was designed for both undergraduate and graduate Human Resource Management courses. The case may be useful in introductory-level human resource management courses, as well as in upper-level talent acquisition or strategic human resource management courses that cover selection. The case has been classroom tested at the undergraduate and graduate levels, in both in-seat and asynchronous online modalities. The case is designed to apply the Attraction-Selection-Attrition (ASA) framework (Schneider, 1987) to guide a selection decision. The case explores three general themes within the ASA framework: understanding overall organizational culture; analyzing organizational skill gaps; and making selection decisions from a pool of imperfect candidates. The case takes a behind-the-scenes look at NFL talent acquisition as an application of the ASA framework.

title: What is a good life: An interpretative qualitative analysis of group discussions from a participatory study with persons with disabilities in rural Uganda
abstractText: Background: People with disabilities in Uganda experience social exclusion, economic marginalisation and structural barriers that negatively impact health and wellbeing. Existing disability research often emphasises functional limitations and clinical outcomes, offering limited insight into how people with disabilities conceptualise a good life. Objectives: This study explored how people with disabilities in rural Uganda define and experience a good life and examined the social, material and relational conditions that enable or constrain its realisation. Method: We conducted a qualitative interpretive study using data from 50 Participatory Learning and Action for Disability (PLA-D) group meetings in Luuka District between December 2024 and February 2025. Meeting minutes documenting collective discussions about what constitutes a good life were analysed thematically using an inductive approach. Results: Participants described a good life as multidimensional and relational, encompassing basic needs, physical and mental health, economic stability, supportive family relationships, social inclusion, safety and community recognition. Dignity, belonging and recognition as valued members of the community were central to wellbeing. However, hunger, poverty, unemployment, stigma, violence, inaccessible infrastructure and limited access to services constrained the realisation of these aspirations. Disability intersected wider structural disadvantage, intensifying vulnerability to poor health, social exclusion and insecurity. Conclusion: People with disabilities in rural Uganda articulated aspirations consistent with broadly shared human goals rather than disability-specific or deficit-oriented expectations but faced additional barriers to achieving them. Contribution: This study contributes context-specific understandings of dignity, belonging and recognition among persons with disabilities in rural Uganda, informing disability-inclusive health and social policies that address structural determinants of wellbeing alongside individual functioning.

title: Maintaining relations: digital communication in university hospitals in the context of the COVID-19 crisis
abstractText: Purpose The COVID-19 crisis intensified digital communication within hospitals. Crisis communication is typically viewed as an instrumental organisational tool for efficient and strategic communication. Adopting a Communication as Constitutive of Organisation (CCO) perspective, this study examines how the entanglement between hospital actors and digital communication provides insights into the continuous constitution of University Hospitals during and beyond the COVID-19 crisis. It considers how evolving sociomaterial interactions reveal matters of concern within crisis communication practices. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a qualitative multiple case study approach, focusing on two University Hospitals in Belgium. A thematic analysis was conducted on focus group discussions from Hosp.A and, using interviews collected at Hosp.B, a second thematic analysis deepened the findings. Findings The findings underscore the significance of “presence” within the hospital's network, demonstrating how digital communication participated in sustaining connections during the crisis. This highlights that the hospital is constituted through interactions and that communicative interaction must be maintained in times of disruption. Digital communication also highlighted the concern for spaces of emotional togetherness within the crisis. After the crisis peak, digital communication was (re)negotiated. This reflects the dynamic relationship between hospital actors and digital communication and highlights the continuous navigation of their place through the matter(s) of concern(s) in the situated realities. Originality/value With a CCO lens, the ongoing (re)negotiation of the sociomaterial entanglement is explored to underpin matter(s) of concern that open avenues for digital crisis communication research and practice.

title: Pengaruh Laba Akuntansi dan Arus Kas Operasi Terhadap Harga Saham Perusahaan Non-Cyclicals di BEI 2020–2025
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh laba akuntansi dan arus kas operasi terhadap harga saham pada perusahaan sektor non-cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020-2025. Metode yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah metode kuantitatif. Teknik pengambilan sampel yang digunakan adalah purposive sampling dengan cara pengambilan sampel menggunakan kriteria tertentu. Data sekunder yang diambil untuk penelitian ini berupa data akuntansi laporan keuangan tahunan perusahaan non-cyclicals di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) tahun 2020-2025. Penelitian ini menggunakan beberapa jenis pengujian, diantaranya uji normalitas data, analisis korelasi pearson product moment, uji korelasi berganda, analisis regresi linier berganda, analisis koefisien determinasi, uji T, dan uji F. Hasil uji t menunjukkan bahwa secara parsial Laba Akuntansi (X1) tidak berpengaruh terhadap Harga Saham (Y), dan Arus Kas Operasi (X2) tidak berpengaruh terhadap Harga Saham (Y). Sedangkan hasil uji f menunjukkan bahwa secara simultan Laba Akuntansi (X1) dan Arus Kas Operasi (X2) secara bersama-sama berpengaruh terhadap Harga Saham (Y) pada perusahaan sektor non-cyclicals yang terdaftar di BEI periode 2020-2025.

title: Automated Credit Risk Assessment for Peer-to-Peer Lending Platforms Using Natural Language Processing on Textual Loan Application Data
abstractText: Peer-to-Peer (P2P) lending platforms have disrupted traditional consumer credit markets by facilitating direct financial transactions between individual retail investors and borrowers. However, evaluating borrower creditworthiness in P2P lending presents severe information asymmetry challenges, as applicants often lack formal credit histories, audited financial statements, or collateral backing. While traditional credit scoring models rely strictly on quantitative financial metrics (e.g., debt-to-income ratio, FICO score, monthly income), they fail to capture qualitative behavioral signals embedded within borrower-authored loan application narratives. This paper presents an automated, multimodal credit risk assessment architecture that integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP) embeddings, psycholinguistic readability metrics, and sentiment analysis with tabular financial indicators to predict borrower default risk. Grounded in non-linear analytical parameterization paradigms and enterprise risk management frameworks, our methodology extracts semantic, emotional, and deception micro-signals from loan description texts using fine-tuned RoBERTa and TF-IDF representations. Evaluated on an empirical dataset of 320,000 P2P loan applications processed across major fintech lending platforms between 2020 and 2026, our multimodal NLP-enriched model achieved an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.898 and an Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (PR-AUC) of 0.852, outperforming traditional financials-only credit scoring models by 14.8%. Integrating textual narrative features reduced Expected Credit Loss (ECL) by $31.2M annually across the portfolio. We present an exhaustive quantitative synthesis incorporating 10 data tables, 10 mathematical behavior graphs, and 20 visually distinct chart architectures detailing linguistic feature importance, default risk distributions, and portfolio yield optimization.

title: A lightweight adaptive dehazing method for unmanned aerial vehicle video
abstractText: Purpose This paper aims to address haze-induced degradation in UAV visual perception, a critical risk to operational safety. The authors propose an engineering-aware, lightweight UAV video dehazing strategy. Design/methodology/approach The authors propose a lightweight strategy integrating OpenCL-accelerated CLAHE in the LAB color space to reduce redundancy. The authors further apply configurable spatial downscaling, frame skipping and asynchronous multithreading to balance visual enhancement and runtime. Findings The proposed lightweight method sustained the 30 fps source cadence in the supplied-video replay without queue drops or processing errors. The default configuration processed every second frame, corresponding to a processing completion rate of 15.00 fps, while the isolated offline timing test achieved 745.5 fps under the specified timing procedure. Practical implications In tested environments with Intel integrated graphics, this approach demonstrates high resource utilization while maintaining continuous processing of the input video. The potential advantages of this approach in physical drone control, obstacle avoidance and downstream decision-making still need to be validated through hardware deployment and task-specific benchmarking. Originality/value The authors conducted an experimental evaluation of the proposed method using a paired image quality assessment scheme and comprehensive, predefined video stability tests. Furthermore, the authors compared it with selected baseline methods in terms of reference-based image similarity, visual enhancement effects, latency and time-domain processing behavior.

title: Impact of nurses’ burnout on patient care at a district hospital: A phenomenological study
abstractText: Background: Burnout among nurses is a critical global issue, particularly in resource-constrained district hospitals in rural Eastern Cape, South Africa. Staff shortages and high workloads contribute to nurse exhaustion and compromised patient care. Qualitative insights into nurses’ lived experiences of burnout in such contexts remain limited. title: Effect of controlled degassing on microstructural, mechanical, and electrochemical properties of NAB castings
abstractText: This study investigates the influence of controlled degassing treatment on the properties of nickel aluminum bronze (NAB) alloy containing 10 wt.% Al, 5 wt.% Ni, 4.8 wt.% Fe, and 1.5 wt.% Mn. Two casting conditions were evaluated: conventional casting (NAB) and degassing-treated casting (NAB-degassed). Microstructural characterization using optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) revealed that degassing treatment resulted in significant microstructural refinement, reduced porosity, and enhanced phase homogeneity. Mechanical evaluation through hardness measurements and wear resistance testing showed that NAB-degassed specimens exhibited superior mechanical properties and improved wear resistance, attributed to refined microstructure and reduced defect density. Electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution demonstrated that degassing markedly enhanced corrosion resistance, with NAB-degassed specimens showing a 55.3 % reduction in corrosion current density (from 2.04 × 10 −5 to 9.12 × 10 −6 A.cm −2) and corrosion rate (from 0.235 to 0.105 mm. year −1). Surface profilometry confirmed improved surface integrity and improved tribological performance. These findings show that controlled degassing treatment is a highly effective approach for optimizing structural integrity and durability of NAB components in severe marine and industrial service conditions.

title: أثر اجتهاد الصحابة على الأحكام الفقهية في زمن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم)
abstractText: يتناول هذا البحث أثر اجتهاد الصحابة رضي الله عنهم على الأحكام الفقهية في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، من خلال دراسة تأصيلية وتطبيقية تجمع بين الجانب الأصولي والجانب الفقهي؛ إذ يهدف إلى بيان حكم اجتهاد الصحابة في العهد النبوي، واستعراض أقوال العلماء في هذه المسألة وأدلتهم ومناقشاتهم، مع تتبع أثر الاجتهادات التي أقرها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في بناء الأحكام والفروع الفقهية لدى المذاهب الفقهية الأربعة. وقد اعتمد البحث منهجًا فقهيًا يقوم على تصوير المسائل وتحرير محل النزاع، وجمع الأقوال ونسبتها إلى أصحابها، وتحليل أدلتها ومناقشتها، ثم الترجيح بينها، مع الاستناد إلى المصادر الحديثية والفقهية والأصولية. وتوصل البحث إلى جواز اجتهاد الصحابة في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، في حضوره وغيابه، وهو ما رجحه الباحث استنادًا إلى الوقائع الثابتة والأدلة الشرعية، وإلى أن اجتهاد الصحابي الذي أقره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكتسب حجية السنة التقريرية. كما بيّن البحث أن المذاهب الفقهية الأربعة أفادت من اجتهادات الصحابة في بناء عدد من المسائل والفروع الفقهية، بما يكشف عن الامتداد التاريخي للاجتهاد في التشريع الإسلامي، وأهمية هذا التراث في فهم الأحكام الفقهية والاستدلال لها. ويوصي البحث بتوسيع الدراسات التطبيقية التي تتتبع اجتهادات الصحابة في أبواب الفقه المختلفة، وإبراز الصلة بين مباحث أصول الفقه وتطبيقاتها العملية، والعناية بتوظيف هذا التراث الاجتهادي في دراسة النوازل الفقهية المعاصرة

Storytelling as a powerful tool for microbiology education in the age of artificial intelligence
abstractText: Designing curricula that engage students and inspire learning about microbiology can be challenging in the era of artificial intelligence (AI). Increasing use of online teaching and AI tools can be distracting and isolating for students at times. By contrast, storytelling connects, teaches, inspires and shapes culture. Equally important, storytelling fosters critical thinking, creativity and self-confidence, which are essential attributes for students to use AI responsibly and ethically. ‘Revolutionary Microbial Discoveries’ is a unit at The University of Western Australia designed to explore the history, current developments and future directions of microbiology. Through storytelling, this unit highlights the historical progression of microbiology and its societal and cultural impacts, distinguishing itself from traditional microbiology courses that primarily focus on biological principles. Student comprehension, engagement and critical thinking skills are fostered by presenting contextualised discoveries and by exploring the transdisciplinary nature of microbiology. Student surveys indicated strong acceptance, with 100% of surveyed students in 2026 reporting that the unit was intellectually stimulating (36% response rate). Alongside the positive feedback, student enrolment numbers doubled within 1 year – from 37 in 2025 to 75 in 2026. This unit has successfully engaged diverse student cohorts by highlighting the importance and impact of microbiology discoveries and by fostering skills essential for engaging with AI such as critical and ethical thinking.

title: Psychometric Validation of the Suicide Attempt Resilience Scale (SRSA-18) in Military Personnel and Members of the Spanish State Security Forces
abstractText: Background: Suicide remains a major public health challenge worldwide and represents a particularly important concern among occupational groups routinely exposed to chronic psychological stress and potentially traumatic events, such as military personnel and members of law enforcement agencies. Identifying protective psychological resources associated with suicide resilience may contribute to more comprehensive suicide prevention strategies. This study examined the psychometric properties of the Suicide Attempt Resilience Scale (SRSA-18) in a sample of military personnel and members of the Spanish State Security Forces. Methods: The study included 166 active-duty professionals (96.39% men; mean [M] = 46.37 years, standard deviation [SD] = 8.35). Internal consistency, factorial structure, and convergent and divergent validity of the SRSA-18 were examined. Confirmatory factor analysis compared the theoretically proposed three-factor model with an alternative one-factor solution. Convergent and divergent validity were assessed through associations with suicidal ideation, depression, anxiety, stress, optimism, perceived social support, cognitive reappraisal, and subjective well-being. Results: The SRSA-18 demonstrated excellent internal consistency for the total score and satisfactory reliability across its three dimensions. The theoretically proposed three-factor model showed a better relative fit than the one-factor solution. However, overall goodness-of-fit indices remained below conventional psychometric standards and provided only limited support for the proposed factorial structure. As expected, suicide resilience was negatively associated with suicidal ideation, depression, anxiety, and stress, and positively associated with optimism, perceived social support, cognitive reappraisal, and subjective wellbeing, supporting the expected pattern of convergent and divergent validity. Conclusions: The present findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the reliability and convergent and divergent validity of the SRSA-18 in military personnel and members of the Spanish State Security Forces. Although the proposed three-factor structure demonstrated better relative performance than a one-factor model, additional psychometric studies using larger and more heterogeneous samples are required to further evaluate its structural validity and determine its applicability across different occupational populations.

title: Hablemos sobre la muerte, ¿por qué no?
abstractText: Objetivo. Sensibilizar e informar acerca de aspectos relativos al final de la vida (documento de instrucciones previas (DIP), cuidados paliativos [CP], muerte) mediante charlas informativas a la población adulta del barrio de Ciudad de los Ángeles de Madrid. Métodos. Experiencia comunitaria. Se han realizado tres charlas del 17 al 29 de octubre de 2024 en el Centro Cultural Bohemios de Villaverde (Madrid). Los temas que contuvieron las sesiones fueron: el documento de instrucciones previas, los CP, la Ley de la Eutanasia, la muerte y el duelo. Participaron de manera voluntaria las personas que se inscribieron a los talleres a través del centro de salud (CS) o el centro cultural. Resultados. La intervención comunitaria incluyó un total de 12 participantes (N = 12). En cuanto a las características sociodemográficas, la muestra estuvo compuesta mayoritariamente por mujeres. La distribución etaria se situó entre los 55 y los 81 años, con predominio del grupo comprendido entre los 60 y los 69 años. El análisis de la asistencia evidenció una reducción acumulada del 33,3% entre la primera y la última sesión. Discusión. La actividad permitió abrir un espacio de diálogo sobre la muerte en la comunidad, disminuyendo prejuicios y favoreciendo la planificación anticipada de decisiones. Aunque la participación fue reducida, la acogida fue positiva y se recomienda repetir la actividad periódicamente. Proponemos comparar con experiencias similares de educación comunitaria en CP para reforzar los hallazgos. Conclusiones. La experiencia demostró que es posible abrir espacios de diálogo comunitario sobre la muerte, favoreciendo la normalización y la planificación anticipada de decisiones. Aunque la asistencia fue limitada, los asistentes valoraron positivamente las charlas. Se recomienda continuar y ampliar estas actividades de forma periódica, con mayor difusión y evaluación formal. Palabras clave: planificación anticipada de decisiones, cuidados paliativos, muerte, duelo, eutanasia.

title: In-tandem electrode implantation for hippocampal deep brain stimulation in refractory temporal lobe epilepsy: technical note
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Hippocampal deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a therapeutic option for selected patients with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) who are not candidates for resection. Conventional hippocampal DBS typically uses a single lead per hippocampus, potentially leaving a substantial portion of the hippocampal body unmodulated. This study aimed to describe the technical feasibility and preliminary clinical outcomes of an in-tandem dual-lead hippocampal DBS implantation technique designed to increase longitudinal hippocampal coverage. METHODS Patients with drug-resistant TLE who were not candidates for resection underwent in-tandem hippocampal DBS. Surgical planning was based on 3-T brain MRI and included 2 target points along the longitudinal hippocampal axis: an anterior point in the hippocampal head and a posterior point in the hippocampal body. Two 8-contact DBS leads were implanted sequentially through a single burr hole, maintaining identical trajectory angles and a 17-mm posterior offset on the stereotactic frame. DBS leads were connected to a dual-channel implantable pulse generator (IPG) in unilateral cases or a 4-channel IPG in bilateral cases. RESULTS In-tandem lead implantation was performed in 8 patients. Adequate hippocampal coverage was achieved in all cases, with at least 14 active contacts positioned within the hippocampus. Six patients underwent at least 1 year of follow-up (mean 24.5 months, range 15–37 months). All 6 patients experienced a more than 50% reduction in seizure frequency: 2 were seizure free (Engel class I), and 4 were Engel class II. No early or late surgical adverse events were observed. CONCLUSIONS In-tandem hippocampal DBS was technically feasible and increased longitudinal hippocampal coverage through a single burr hole per side while providing additional stimulation and programming options. The favorable seizure outcomes observed in this small uncontrolled cohort are preliminary and do not establish superiority over conventional single-lead hippocampal DBS. Larger prospective comparative studies are needed to determine whether increased anatomical coverage for DBS in refractory TLE improves seizure control.

title: A BIM-based framework for reliability-constrained cost minimization of electromechanical systems under seismic uncertainty in early design
abstractText: Purpose This study develops a proactive methodology that integrates probabilistic seismic assessment into building information modeling (BIM) during early design. While BIM is widely used for design management, its potential for component-level reliability-based seismic evaluation remains underexplored. Design/methodology/approach A BIM-based probabilistic framework was developed to support the reliability-constrained cost minimization (RCCM) of mechanical and electrical (M&E) component configurations under seismic uncertainty. The framework integrates fragility curves and seismic hazard characterization into a unified decision-support model to select the lowest-cost feasible M&E component configuration that satisfies user-defined reliability thresholds during early design. The framework is demonstrated through a case study of the early design of a backup power system in a sewage pumping station. The case study is followed by complementary sensitivity analyses that examine how variations in site-specific seismic hazards, reliability requirements and the median fragility parameter θ influence component selection. The implementation uses Python scripts within Dynamo to process location-specific hazard information and evaluate reliability-based alternatives directly within the BIM workflow. Findings Results indicate that embedding probabilistic seismic assessment in BIM enhances early design decision-making by enabling the visualization of reliability-based outcomes and cost-informed component selection. In low-hazard areas, unanchored generator configurations satisfy the defined reliability requirements, whereas in high-hazard areas, anchored configurations are required to achieve the required performance level. Sensitivity testing of the median fragility parameter θ further reveals that RCCM-based selection remains stable under low and moderate reliability requirements but becomes more sensitive under high reliability requirements. Research limitations/implications The framework assumes uniform ground-level seismic input and does not incorporate floor-dependent seismic demand or interstory dynamic effects. Practical implications The approach supports cost-effective, data-driven selection of resilient components in seismic-prone environments. Originality/value This research introduces a framework that integrates probabilistic seismic analysis within BIM during early design, linking analytical modeling with practical visualization and decision support. Its main contribution lies in translating coupled seismic hazard and component fragility information into reliability-constrained, cost-informed component selection within a BIM-based workflow.

Economic Growth, Energy Consumption, Urbanization, and Ecological Footprint in ASEAN: A Panel Analysis
abstractText: This study examines how economic growth, energy consumption, and urbanization are associated with the per capita ecological footprint in eight Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) members during 2010–2022, where ecological pressure varies sharply and earlier evidence is inconsistent. An observational associative design was applied to a balanced panel of 104 country-year observations from the World Bank and the Global Footprint Network. The Chow and Hausman tests selected the Fixed Effect Model, followed by diagnostic and robustness checks. In the main model, economic growth (annual GDP per capita growth, %), energy consumption (kilograms of oil equivalent per capita), and urbanization (urban population, % of total) were each positively associated with the ecological footprint (global hectares, gha, per capita) at the 5% level and jointly (Wald F = 16.27, p < 0.001). Holding the other variables constant, a one-percentage-point higher growth rate, a one-percentage-point higher urban share, and an additional 100 kilograms of oil equivalent per capita were associated with 0.012, 0.014, and 0.069 gha per capita more footprint, respectively. These are statistical associations, not causal effects. Energy consumption was the most robust association across alternative specifications, whereas the significance of growth and urbanization depended on the standard-error estimator. The results are consistent with development still being accompanied by rising ecological pressure while energy remains fossil-fuel dependent, although the design cannot identify this mechanism. Improving energy efficiency and accelerating the shift to renewable energy are the best-supported policy priorities, with sustainable urban planning as a supporting measure.

title: Low-intensity focused ultrasound for epilepsy: a scoping review toward circuit-level neuromodulation and parameter discovery
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) has emerged as a promising noninvasive neuromodulatory approach for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). However, the sonication parameters required to produce reliable and durable neuromodulatory effects remain poorly defined. Therefore, the authors aimed to perform a scoping review of preclinical and clinical studies investigating LIFU for epilepsy to characterize the sonication parameter space and examine the potential role of intracranial EEG in advancing circuit-level parameter discovery. METHODS A scoping review was performed in accordance with PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. Articles investigating LIFU applications in epilepsy that were indexed in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library between 2010 and 2026 were included. Extracted data included study design, epilepsy model or patient population, ultrasound platforms, neural targets, sonication parameters, therapeutic outcomes, electrophysiological and imaging findings, and adverse events. Active clinical trials investigating LIFU for DRE were also reviewed. RESULTS Twenty-nine studies (25 preclinical and 4 clinical investigations) that met inclusion criteria and 8 registered clinical trials were assessed. Across animal models and early human studies, LIFU targeting the hippocampus and thalamus was associated with reductions in epileptiform activity, seizure frequency, and network-level electrophysiological changes. Clinical studies demonstrated the feasibility and relative safety of repeated transcranial sonication, including one study integrating LIFU with simultaneous stereo-EEG that showed spatially localized spectral modulation at seizure-onset zone electrodes. Sonication protocols varied substantially. Fundamental frequencies ranged 200–1500 kHz, duty cycles (DCs) ranged 1%–80%, and spatial-peak temporal-average intensity (ISPTA) values ranged from 100 mW/cm 2 in preclinical studies to 2800 mW/cm 2 in therapeutic cohorts. Bidirectional neuromodulatory effects, including seizure exacerbation, were linked to specific parameter combinations, particularly shorter interstimulus intervals. Lower DC protocols were most consistently associated with inhibitory and antiseizure effects, while repeated-session paradigms generally produced more durable seizure suppression. Early clinical trials showed preliminary trends toward frequencies of 548–650 kHz, DCs of 18%–30%, ISPTA ceilings of 2800 mW/cm 2, and multisession treatment paradigms. CONCLUSIONS LIFU represents a novel noninvasive modality for modulating epileptic networks and expanding the therapeutic landscape for DRE. However, optimization of sonication parameters remains a major translational challenge. Integration of LIFU with intracranial EEG, including stereo-EEG, deep brain stimulation, and responsive neurostimulation, might facilitate biomarker-guided parameter discovery, mechanistic investigation, and circuit-level therapy development. Further standardized preclinical and prospective clinical investigations are necessary to establish effective sonication paradigms and evaluate long-term safety and therapeutic efficacy.

title: Effect of Club-Style Psychological Counselling Service on Anxiety and Depression in Patients With Haematology Undergoing Chemotherapy With Totally Implantable Venous Access Port
abstractText: Background: To explore the associations between club-style psychological counselling and anxiety, depression, treatment compliance, quality of life (QoL) and totally implantable venous access port (TIVAP)-related adverse events in patients with haematological diseases undergoing TIVAP chemotherapy. Methods: This retrospective observational cohort study included 146 patients (January 2024–October 2025). Participants were allocated into the observation group (70 cases, routine nursing + club-style psychological counselling) and control group (76 cases, routine nursing alone) according to recorded medical resource accessibility and patients’ voluntary service selection. Data were extracted from electronic medical records, nursing documents and psychological assessment records. Assessments were conducted at baseline (1–2 days pre-first chemotherapy), 4-week follow-up, and study end (1–2 days postlast chemotherapy) using Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), a self-developed treatment compliance scale, and European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer QoL Questionnaire-Core 30 (QLQ-C30). TIVAP-related adverse events were also recorded. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Bonferroni correction was used to compare changes over time and between groups. Missing data were processed via multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) and complete-case sensitivity analysis. Outcome assessors were blinded to group assignment during original scale evaluation. Results: At baseline, no significant between-group differences were observed in all indicators between groups (p > 0.05). At 4-week follow-up and study end, GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores in the observation group were significantly lower than their respective baseline values and those of the control group at matched time points (all adjusted p < 0.001, Cohen’s d > 0.80). The control group showed no significant changes in GAD-7 or PHQ-9 scores across time points (p > 0.05). At study end, the observation group had higher treatment compliance scores [(52.42 ± 4.15) vs. (45.22 ± 5.25), p < 0.001], better QLQ-C30 functional dimension scores, and lower symptom dimension scores (post-hoc adjusted p < 0.001). No significant between-group difference was found in the incidence of TIVAP-related adverse events (4.3% vs. 6.6%, Fisher’s exact test p = 0.807). Conclusions: This retrospective cohort study only reveals correlative differences rather than causal effects. Club-style psychological counselling was correlated with milder anxiety and depression, higher treatment compliance, and better QoL among patients with haematological diseases receiving TIVAP chemotherapy, without correlating with elevated TIVAP adverse event risk. The multi-component service model provides exploratory real-world evidence for clinical psychological nursing optimisation; however, the inherent study limitations restrict causal inference and generalisability.

title: Crystal structure and supramolecular interactions in a mixed-ligand zinc(II) salicylate–neocuproine complex
abstractText: A mixed-ligand zinc(II) complex, Zn(Sal) 2 (Neo), where Sal denotes the monoanionic salicylate ligand and Neo denotes neocuproine (2,9-dimethyl-1,10-phenanthroline), was synthesised and characterised by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The complex crystallises in P 2 1 / n and exhibits a distorted ZnN 2 O 3 coordination environment comprising four short Zn–donor contacts and a longer Zn–O contact of 2.458(4) Å. The salicylate ligands display monodentate and asymmetric bidentate carboxylate coordination. Intermolecular C–H⋯O contacts and aromatic stacking contribute to the crystal packing. Hirshfeld surface analysis identifies H⋯H, C⋯H/H⋯C and O⋯H/H⋯O contributions of 35.0 %, 26.1 % and 24.9 %, respectively. Pairwise interaction energies distinguish contact abundance from energetic importance: dispersion is the largest attractive component for every tabulated molecular pair. QTAIM analysis identifies five Zn–donor bond critical points, with the lowest electron density at one Zn–O contact. These results distinguish the unequal metal–oxygen interactions and the dispersive contribution to intermolecular association in this mixed-ligand structure.

title: Sensitivity of Hubble-constant estimates to possible distortions of Cepheid period–luminosity relations
abstractText: We investigate the sensitivity of Cepheid-based estimates of the Hubble constant to possible nonlinearities and distance-dependent distortions of Cepheid period--luminosity relations (PLRs). Using previously published Cepheid and supernova (SN) data, we compared straight-line and continuous piecewise-linear representations of the PLR, original and binned Cepheid samples, and inverse-variance and equal weighting of SN hosts. Motivated by the observed increase in PLR scatter with host distance, we used a simple toy model to examine whether increasing observational noise can bias PLR slopes derived using ordinary least squares (OLS) and, in combination with differences in the period distributions of anchor and SN-host samples, propagate into the inferred distances. We then explored this effect using a phenomenological distance-dependent parameterization of the fitted PLR coefficients. The SN-host data show a statistically significant increase in the observed PLR scatter with distance at the 3.2--3.3σ level, whereas the corresponding trend in the fitted PLR slope remains below 2σ. Representing the global PLR as a broken line gives exploratory Cepheid-based estimates of H_0 in the range 70.5--71.5, . Additionally allowing for a phenomenological distance-dependent observational bias in the fitted PLR coefficients, motivated by the observed increase in PLR scatter with distance and its possible effect on OLS fitting, yields values of approximately 67--74, for different reference distances. -1 ,Mpc^ -1 -1 ,Mpc^ -1 The inferred value of H_0 is sensitive both to the PLR functional form---a single straight line versus a continuous piecewise-linear relation---and to observational effects that increase with distance and can bias OLS-derived coefficients. The 67--74, range obtained for different reference distances is not a new measurement, but indicates the scale of the shift possible within this exploratory framework. More homogeneous anchor data and photometric reductions are needed to reduce these effects and assess their impact on the Cepheid distance scale and inferred H_0. -1 ,Mpc^ -1

title: Rediscovery and redescription of the enigmatic Central European ant-like stone beetle Neuraphes slovenicus Machulka (Coleoptera, Staphylinidae, Scydmaeninae)
abstractText: Neuraphes (s. str.) slovenicus Machulka was described in 1931 based on a single male collected in eastern Slovakia, and since then has been recorded without any details also from Ukraine in keys and catalogues. We report a recent finding of three specimens in a different region of Slovakia. Based on the holotype and the newly collected material, N. slovenicus is redescribed, and its aedeagus is illustrated for the first time. This species was misidentified in the widely used identification manual to Central European beetles Die Käfer Mitteleuropas, and the record from Ukraine is erroneous.

title: Fractal-Fractional Calculus: The Exact Inverse Operator for Caputo-Type Derivatives and Its Role in Modeling Complex Systems
abstractText: This paper develops the Atangana fractal-fractional integral as the integral companion associated with Caputo-type fractal-fractional derivatives with power-law, exponential-decay, and Mittag-Leffler kernels. The corresponding integral operators are derived directly from the defining Cauchy problems, and the fundamental composition relations are established for each kernel. For the singular power-law kernel, direct inversion is obtained, whereas the nonsingular exponential and Mittag-Leffler kernels retain intrinsic initial-memory contributions determined by the kernel and the value of the input function at the lower terminal. Several structural properties of the resulting operators are established, including factorization, boundedness, derivative-free representations, and exact action on power functions. For the power-law case, a global existence and uniqueness result is proved for nonlinear fractal-fractional Cauchy problems without imposing a smallness restriction on the final time interval. A structure-preserving numerical method based on piecewise-linear interpolation is then constructed directly from the Atangana fractal-fractional integral. The method preserves positivity and exact operator moments and is proved to be globally stable and second-order convergent for sufficiently smooth composed forcing. Numerical examples with vanishing and nonvanishing initial forcing confirm the theoretical convergence rate. The results provide a consistent analytical and computational framework linking Caputo-type fractal-fractional differentiation with its associated integral structure.
